HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from health signal to one risk, its evidence, owner, and next intervention.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If status data is unavailable, work from what people know and note where the evidence should have come from.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name one technical risk, its evidence, its owner, and the next intervention.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Find one technical health risk that is not visible in the data, and take it to its owner.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the risk, where the signal came from, and who now owns it.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: Value without evidence tends to read as opinion. Today is about the evidence, and who needs to hear it.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints:
The customer defines value. Our job is to evidence it in their terms.
Causality is easy to claim and hard to support. Say what the data supports.
A value story nobody hears is not value realized.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions:
Which technical progress has not yet been translated into customer value?
Which cost, consumption, or optimization signal is credible enough to use?
What claim would you refuse to make without stronger evidence?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one optimization, consumption, or delivery-progress signal and the outcome it might support.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions:
Which optimization or progress signal could become a value story?
What financial or technical claim requires review?
What evidence is missing before recommending action?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Through the CSA lens, listen for: invented savings; correlation presented as causality; optimization divorced from architecture tradeoffs; and value claims not tied to supported outcomes.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from the signal to one bounded recommendation or technical value narrative.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If evidence sources are unavailable, build the value structure and identify what evidence you would need.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Commit to to one evidence-backed optimization or technical value recommendation.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Evidence one technical outcome in terms the customer would use themselves.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the outcome, the evidence, and how you phrased it.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: Value without evidence tends to read as opinion. Today is about the evidence, and who needs to hear it.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints:
The customer defines value. Our job is to evidence it in their terms.
Causality is easy to claim and hard to support. Say what the data supports.
A value story nobody hears is not value realized.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions:
What value story would the customer actually recognize?
Which evidence supports the story, and which part is still only expected?
What next technical action would make the value more real?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one technical review, business review, or value-realization example and the evidence behind it.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions:
Which customer review package would benefit from AI assembly?
What evidence must travel with the value story?
Which next technical action makes the value more credible?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Through the CSA lens, listen for: progress not connected to agreed outcomes; unsupported realization claims; missing source links; and follow-through that lacks owners.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from value language to the evidence package and next technical action.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If evidence sources are unavailable, build the value structure and identify what evidence you would need.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Commit to to one technical value story and the evidence that will travel with it.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Produce one costed optimization recommendation the customer could act on this quarter.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the recommendation, the cost basis, and the customer response.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: This is the session that explains the motion through the CSAM lens: less status assembly, more customer outcome leadership.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints: Huddles are 30 minutes and workflow-led. CSAM work stays human-led: AI helps gather, synthesize, draft and monitor; the CSAM validates context, trust, commitments and customer-facing messages.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions:
Which part of your week is assembling information rather than deciding anything?
Where do you already use AI, and where have you avoided it?
What would you need to see before you trusted an AI-drafted customer success output?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: confirm access to the tools named for this path, and come ready to describe the work you repeat most weeks. No prior AI experience is needed for this session.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions:
Which customer success work do you repeat every week without thinking of it as a workflow?
Which of those steps is assembling information rather than making a decision?
Where must the CSAM judgment stay human no matter how good the output gets?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for unvoiced scepticism, access blockers stated as disinterest, the assumption that this is a tool rollout, and people who describe only their exceptional work rather than the work they repeat. The recurring, unglamorous tasks are the ones worth mapping.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from how the motion works to the recurring work each person will map with the discovery prompt this week.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If tool access is not confirmed, still run the discovery conversation and record access blockers separately from interest. The discovery prompt can be run in whichever tool the person already has.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Close by pointing the team to the resources for next week's topic and to the workflow-discovery prompt below. Week 1 is for finding the recurring work worth automating.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: Which part of your week had you never thought of as a workflow until now? What would have to be true before you trusted AI with it?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt:
Run this in Microsoft 365 Copilot, Cowork, or Scout before the next huddle, then bring the result to the session:

"I am a Customer Success Account Manager at Microsoft and I want to find the recurring work in my week that AI could take on.
1. First, look at my calendar, mail and Teams activity from the last four weeks and tell me what you can see about where my time actually goes. If you cannot access that data, say so and move to step 2 rather than guessing.
2. Then ask me up to five short questions, one at a time, to cover the work that never shows up in a calendar or an inbox.
3. Then list the five things I do most often. For each one give an estimate of the time it costs me per month, whether it is best handled as a saved prompt, a reusable skill, a scheduled automation or an existing agent, and the one judgment that must stay mine.
4. Rank them by time returned and tell me which one to start with."
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the ranked list of the five things you repeat most, which of them looked like a prompt, skill, automation, or agent fit, and any AI experience from the week, including anything that did not work.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: Success planning is not documentation. It is how the customer and Microsoft agree what progress means.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints: A plan should name outcomes, milestones, owners, risks and review points. AI can draft and inspect the plan, but only the CSAM can validate the customer priority and commitment.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions:
When did your success plan last change because the customer's priorities changed?
Which milestone in it would the customer not recognize as theirs?
What is in the plan because it is genuinely the outcome, and what is there because it was easy to measure?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one active customer priority, its current CSP or success-plan notes and the latest review or action list.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions:
Which outcome in your plan is stated in the customer's words rather than ours?
Which milestone has drifted without anyone deciding to move it?
What would you remove from the plan today to make it governable?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for plans built around Microsoft milestones rather than customer outcomes, measures chosen because they are available rather than meaningful, owners who have never agreed to their commitment, and plans so long that nobody governs them. Also listen for drift being reported rather than decided.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from the plan as it stands to the single outcome you will make observable this week.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If the tool or data source is unavailable, map the current workflow manually, name the trusted sources and draft the prompt plus human checkpoint for later testing.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name the customer, the one outcome you will make observable this week, and what you will remove from the plan to keep it governable.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Make one success plan outcome observable this week, and remove something to keep the plan governable.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the outcome you made measurable and what you removed.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: Today is about moving from signal review to intervention. Scores help, but action changes the customer trajectory.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints: Health work spans adoption, usage, support, delivery, sentiment and stakeholder change. The CSAM must separate noise from the risk that matters most right now.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions:
Which customer worries you for reasons the health score does not capture?
What did someone say in a recent conversation that has not made it into any system?
Which risk have you been watching rather than acting on, and why?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one account with visible health, adoption, support or delivery risk and the current owner or open question.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions:
What is the driver behind the score, not the score itself?
Which signal came from a person rather than a system, and did it survive into the record?
Who owns the intervention, and by when does it have to start to matter?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for health scores treated as the diagnosis rather than the symptom, risks the team has normalized, interventions without owners, and conversation-based signals that never reached the data. Also listen for the customer's own view of their health being absent from the discussion.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from the ranked health view to one intervention with an owner, a due date, and an escalation threshold.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If the tool or data source is unavailable, map the current workflow manually, name the trusted sources and draft the prompt plus human checkpoint for later testing.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name the top risk, its actual driver rather than its score, the owner who has agreed to the intervention, and the escalation threshold.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Find the driver behind one health score, then take the intervention to an owner who agrees to it.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the driver, the owner, and the escalation threshold you set.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: Executive alignment is where customer success becomes visible to the people who can sponsor, unblock or redirect it.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints: Stakeholder maps should show influence, decision rights, relationship health and the next ask. AI can assemble signals; the CSAM decides the message and timing.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions:
Who is the most senior person at this customer you have never spoken to directly?
Which stakeholder could stop this work, and do you know what they care about?
When an executive last engaged, what did they actually want from us?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one upcoming executive or sponsor conversation and the latest stakeholder context.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions:
Which stakeholder can stop this, and what do they need to believe?
Where is your coverage a title on a map rather than a relationship?
What would you ask the executive for if you had fifteen minutes tomorrow?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for stakeholder maps built from org charts rather than observed behavior, executive relationships that exist only through an intermediary, engagement plans with no ask, and blockers identified without a plan to reach them. Also listen for assuming a quiet stakeholder is a supportive one.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from the stakeholder map to the one relationship you will build this month and the reason they would take the meeting.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If the tool or data source is unavailable, map the current workflow manually, name the trusted sources and draft the prompt plus human checkpoint for later testing.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name the stakeholder you will reach this month, what that person needs to believe, and who can make the introduction.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Reach one stakeholder you have never spoken to directly, and know what they care about before you do.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring who you reached, how, and what you learned that you did not expect.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: CSAM orchestration is making the customer-success system observable enough to run.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints: Handoffs need an input, owner and date. Escalation is not a failure when it is used to unblock the system and protect customer outcomes.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions:
Where does work currently stop between Microsoft, the partner, and the customer?
Who believes they own something that someone else also believes they own?
Which handoff have you personally been compensating for?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one workstream involving Microsoft, customer, partner, support or delivery handoffs.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions:
Where exactly does work stop between the three parties?
Who thinks they own that step, and have you asked them?
What are you personally absorbing because the handoff does not work?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for the CSAM compensating for a broken handoff rather than fixing it, ownership assumed across company boundaries, partner commitments with no date, and coordination meetings that report rather than decide. Also listen for the customer's own team being left out of the orchestration picture.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from the coordination map to the one handoff you will make explicit, with both sides named.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If the tool or data source is unavailable, map the current workflow manually, name the trusted sources and draft the prompt plus human checkpoint for later testing.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name the handoff you will make explicit, both parties by name, and the date it will be agreed rather than assumed.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Make one handoff explicit this week by agreeing it with both sides rather than assuming it.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the handoff, both owners, and the date it was agreed.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: Adoption activity does not automatically become customer value. Today is about proving and accelerating value realization.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints: Adoption plans should link underused features, customer priorities, behavior-change actions, milestones and value evidence. AI can draft the plan and value narrative; the CSAM validates truth and relevance.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions:
What value has this customer actually realized that you could prove today?
Where is adoption stalled, and do you know why or are you guessing?
What would the customer say they got, if asked without us in the room?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one workload or solution where adoption progress, friction or value proof needs to be clarified.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions:
What value can you evidence today, and what are you asserting?
Where adoption stalled, do you know the cause or are you inferring it?
Would the customer describe the value the same way you just did?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for value claimed from usage figures alone, adoption barriers guessed rather than investigated, realized value described in Microsoft terms rather than customer outcomes, and proof that would not survive a procurement conversation. Also listen for value stories that have never been said back to the customer.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from the value picture to one claim you will evidence, and one adoption barrier you will actually diagnose.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If the tool or data source is unavailable, map the current workflow manually, name the trusted sources and draft the prompt plus human checkpoint for later testing.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name one value claim you will evidence, one adoption barrier you will diagnose rather than guess at, and how you will say it back to the customer.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Evidence one value claim, and diagnose one adoption barrier instead of guessing at it.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the evidenced claim and what you found was actually blocking adoption.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: Renewal readiness starts before the renewal motion. Today is about seeing risk and growth conditions early.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints: Consumption, MACC or usage trajectory, adoption gaps, value evidence, support health and stakeholder signals all shape renewal confidence.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions:
Which renewal are you least confident about, and what specifically drives that?
What consumption signal would you want to see six months before a renewal conversation?
Where is growth genuinely available versus where are you hoping?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one account with renewal, consumption, usage or expansion relevance in the near planning horizon.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions:
What is your forecast based on, and how far ahead does the signal reach?
Which growth opportunity is supported by consumption evidence?
What would you need to know now to avoid a surprise at renewal?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for forecasts driven by relationship confidence rather than consumption evidence, growth assumed from headroom rather than intent, renewal risk surfacing late because nobody looked early, and commercial ownership blurring between CSAM and CE. Also listen for consumption trends read without seasonality.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from the forecast to the one early signal you will start tracking, and who you will align it with.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If the tool or data source is unavailable, map the current workflow manually, name the trusted sources and draft the prompt plus human checkpoint for later testing.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name the renewal you are least confident about, the early signal you will start tracking, and who you will align the forecast with.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Start tracking one early consumption signal and hand it to the account owner.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the signal, why it matters, and who you handed it to.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: Escalations test trust. Today is about moving from scattered status to a grounded recovery plan.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints: A useful brief names customer impact, current status, owner, decision needed, next action and update cadence. AI can consolidate threads; the CSAM validates tone, accuracy and accountability.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions:
What issue are you currently managing that should probably already be escalated?
What is holding you back: evidence, ownership, or the conversation itself?
When an escalation last worked well, what made it work?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one live or recent delivery risk, incident, support issue or overdue commitment.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions:
What threshold would have told you to escalate this a month ago?
What does the recovery plan commit us to, and can we deliver it?
What will you tell the customer, and when?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for escalation delayed to avoid an uncomfortable conversation, recovery plans that promise more than delivery can support, customer communication planned after the internal fix rather than alongside it, and escalations raised without a defined exit. Also listen for the same issue recurring without anyone treating the pattern.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from the delivery risk to a recovery plan with an owner, a customer message, and a defined exit condition.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If the tool or data source is unavailable, map the current workflow manually, name the trusted sources and draft the prompt plus human checkpoint for later testing.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name the risk you will escalate or resolve this week, the recovery commitment delivery can actually support, and what the customer will be told.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Take one issue to escalation or resolution this week, with a recovery commitment delivery can actually support.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the issue, the recovery plan, and what the customer was told.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: Investment should be connected to a real customer barrier, not added as a side process. Today is about the AE’s role in naming the investment hypothesis and routing the next decision.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints: Eligibility, funding, and approval are governed human decisions. AI may help assemble context, status, and evidence, but the AE should not overstate approval or commitment.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions: Where could investment remove a barrier? Which part is yours to advance? Who owns the next governed decision?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one live opportunity or account barrier where investment may be relevant, plus any approved context you can safely use.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions: Where might investment remove a real barrier? What evidence supports that barrier? Who owns eligibility, funding, approval, delivery, or value proof?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for funding implied as approved, hidden open questions, unowned handoffs, and investment ideas not tied to an account priority or decision.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from investment concept to the AE’s next governed action on one live case.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: Use a sanitized scenario if live data is not appropriate. Do not infer eligibility, approval, or funding status.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name the investment hypothesis, evidence gap, and next governed owner.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Test whether investment could remove one real barrier, then route the next decision without implying approval.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the investment hypothesis, source evidence, open questions, owner, and the next governed action.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: AE orchestration works when everyone knows the customer decision, their role, the handoff, and the date. Today is about making that operating model explicit.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints: AEs often lead through influence without direct authority. AI can assemble commitments, role gaps, partner context, and follow-up drafts; the AE decides who to pull in and how to lead the motion.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions: Where is the handoff currently vague? Which role or partner is missing? What would reduce follow-up noise this week?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one live account or opportunity that depends on multiple Microsoft roles, partners, or delivery handoffs.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions: Which role, partner, or handoff is missing right now? What input does each owner need? What follow-up should be automated or drafted, and what should remain relationship-led?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for responsibility without authority, handoffs assumed rather than confirmed, partner motions added late, and meetings where every role attends but no owner is clear.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from role discussion to an owner/date/input map for one opportunity.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If systems are unavailable, map the handoff chain manually and capture the prompt or workflow to run later.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name one handoff, role gap, or partner action you will make explicit this week.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Create or update one account-team operating brief with owners, inputs, dates, and next customer decision.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the role/partner map, handoff list, follow-up message or plan, and what changed after owner validation.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: A QBR or executive cadence should not be a status meeting. It should make value, commitments, risks, and strategic asks visible enough for the customer to decide.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints: AI can assemble outcomes, usage signals, open commitments, risks, investments, and expansion plays. The AE validates what the customer would recognize as value and which ask advances the relationship.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions: What value has been delivered but not evidenced? Which customer commitment is still open? What strategic ask should the QBR create?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one account with a QBR, SBR, renewal, or executive follow-up where value evidence matters.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions: What value would the customer recognize? Which outcome is supported by evidence, and which is only expected? What strategic ask should follow from the value story?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for value claims without evidence, QBRs that become status readouts, unsupported causality, missing customer commitments, and expansion asks not tied to outcomes.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from value evidence to the executive brief or QBR ask the AE would actually use.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If evidence sources are unavailable, build the value structure and mark each claim as supported, assumed, or needs review.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name one value claim to evidence and one strategic ask to sharpen.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Build one executive value or QBR brief and validate which claims are supported before sharing.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the value/QBR brief, source evidence, unsupported claims removed, strategic asks, and owner for follow-up.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: Today is about assess the strategic and technical case for investment without turning the huddle into a tool demo or a status review.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints: The goal is A strategic and technical investment assessment with dependencies, readiness, risks, and the next governed decision named. AI can assemble evidence and draft options, but ATS judgment stays accountable for strategy, technical accuracy, and next decisions.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions:
What technical problem is this investment actually meant to solve?
What would tell you six months from now that it worked?
Which dependency would quietly sink it, and who owns that dependency?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: confirm access to the named tools, bring one real account or technical strategy example, and review the commitment from the prior huddle.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions:
What technical outcome does this investment buy that we could not get otherwise?
What is the observable measure that proves it worked?
Which approval or eligibility question are you assuming rather than confirming?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for the ATS drifting into eligibility, funding, or approval decisions that belong to other owners, success measures that cannot be observed, deployment paths assumed rather than validated, and handoffs to delivery with no re-engagement trigger.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from the investment case to the technical evidence it needs and the governed decision that comes next.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If tooling is unavailable, map the workflow and human checkpoint manually, then draft the prompt for later testing.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name the investment, the observable success measure, and the approval question you will route to its correct owner rather than answering themselves.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Test one investment case against its technical dependencies, and route one approval question to its real owner.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the dependency that would sink it and the owner you routed the question to.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: Today is about prepare the technical contribution for a customer business review without turning the huddle into a tool demo or a status review.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints: The goal is A technical CBR contribution with roadmap points, evidence, risks, decisions, and follow-through. AI can assemble evidence and draft options, but ATS judgment stays accountable for strategy, technical accuracy, and next decisions.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions:
What technical progress can you evidence, rather than assert?
Where has progress been slower than the customer expected, and how will you say so?
What decision do you want the review to produce?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: confirm access to the named tools, bring one real account or technical strategy example, and review the commitment from the prior huddle.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions:
Which technical claim in your contribution can you evidence today?
How will you present the area where progress was slower than promised?
What decision should this review produce, and who makes it?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for progress narrated rather than evidenced, slow areas omitted rather than addressed, roadmap statements that commit the product group, and reviews that end without a decision. Also listen for a technical contribution disconnected from the business outcome the customer cares about.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from the technical contribution to the decisions it should trigger, and the evidence each decision requires.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If tooling is unavailable, map the workflow and human checkpoint manually, then draft the prompt for later testing.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name the technical claim you will evidence before the review, and the slow area you will address openly rather than omit.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Evidence one technical claim before your next customer review, and decide how you will address the slowest area.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the evidenced claim and how you handled the area that is behind.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: Today is about assess technical health and prioritize risk response without turning the huddle into a tool demo or a status review.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints: The goal is A prioritized technical risk response with source signals, owner, intervention, and checkpoint. AI can assemble evidence and draft options, but ATS judgment stays accountable for strategy, technical accuracy, and next decisions.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions:
Which technical risk have you known about for weeks without acting on?
What is stopping you: evidence, ownership, or the conversation itself?
Which risk would the customer say is most urgent, and does it match yours?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: confirm access to the named tools, bring one real account or technical strategy example, and review the commitment from the prior huddle.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions:
Which risk is most likely to become an escalation, and what is the earliest signal?
Who owns the intervention, and have they agreed to it?
What would you tell the customer today if you had to raise this now?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for risks ranked by score rather than by consequence, interventions with no named owner, escalation thresholds that were never defined, and risks the team has normalized because they have lived with them. Also listen for signals from conversations that never made it into the system data.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from the ranked risk view to one intervention with an owner, a date, and an escalation threshold.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If tooling is unavailable, map the workflow and human checkpoint manually, then draft the prompt for later testing.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name the top technical risk, the intervention, the owner who has agreed to it, and the threshold that would trigger escalation.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Take one technical risk to its owner this week with the intervention and the escalation threshold.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the risk, the owner who accepted it, and the threshold you agreed.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: Investment-funded proof work needs scope, success measures, failure-mode awareness, and handoff boundaries before execution begins.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints:
SE owns the technical clarity, not eligibility, policy, commercial, or approval decisions.
Success measures must be observable.
Delivery handoff should state what is decided, what remains open, and when SE must be re-engaged.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions:
What technical problem is the investment meant to prove or unblock?
Which success measure is observable enough?
What failure mode would make the investment underdeliver?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Bring a proposed investment-funded proof, workshop, PoC, or scoped engagement and the current technical assumptions.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions:
Which technical scope boundary matters most?
Which success measure proves the investment helped?
What failure mode or handoff gap needs to be closed before review?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for eligibility or approval decisions implied by the SE, vague proof measures, hidden open questions, and delivery handoffs without re-engagement triggers.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from investment idea to bounded technical proof package.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If live data is inappropriate, use a sanitized case and do not infer eligibility, funding, policy, or approval status.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Commit to to one scoped technical proof artifact, success measure, or delivery handoff update.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Define what one investment-funded proof must demonstrate, in measures someone else could verify.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the success measures and the failure mode you named.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: Investment succeeds on role clarity, evidence, and clean handoffs. Today is about the commercial and policy link in that chain.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints: Eligibility, funding, exception, and approval remain human decisions. The CE contribution is to surface commercial and policy dependencies, cite authoritative guidance, and route questions to the right owner.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions: Which commercial dependency would slow this investment later? Which decision is genuinely yours? Which question must be routed to an authoritative owner?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one proposed or in-flight investment, customer agreement context, current policy question, and the known owner or approver.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions: Which activity helps clarify the commercial or policy dependency? What would make the output safe to use? Where must a human owner decide?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for: eligibility, funding, or approval implied rather than decided; exception ownership unclear; handoffs without named owners; and questions that need authoritative guidance.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from the investment lifecycle to the CE-owned dependency and the next governed action.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: Use a sanitized scenario. Do not use live customer data or infer eligibility, approval, exception, or funding status.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Map one investment dependency to the authoritative question, owner, and next human decision.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Map the approval dependencies for one investment and find where it is actually waiting.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the dependency map and the blocker you identified.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: Investment succeeds on role clarity, evidence and clean handoffs. Today is about your part of that chain.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints:
Every role owns one link. The chain breaks at the handoff.
Eligibility, funding and approval are human decisions. AI assembles the evidence.
An investment request without named open questions hides them rather than resolving them.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions:
Where could investment-funded scope become undeliverable?
Which prerequisite, dependency, or owner must be confirmed before delivery starts?
What technical outcome evidence will be needed later?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one proposed or approved investment-funded scope, known technical dependencies, and the delivery checkpoints you would want confirmed.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions:
Which investment activity is closest to your real delivery responsibility?
What status or milestone data must be verified before acting?
Where could handoff, prerequisite, or ownership failure become customer-visible?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Through the CSA lens, listen for: funding or approval inferred from summaries; delivery status not checked against the authoritative record; unowned prerequisites; and technical outcomes that cannot be measured later.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from the investment lifecycle to the CSA's delivery-readiness or outcome-evidence action on a live or sanitized case.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: Use a sanitized scenario. Do not use live customer data or infer eligibility, approval or funding status.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name one investment delivery-readiness check or outcome-evidence action and its owner.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Validate delivery readiness for one investment and name the dependency most likely to slip.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the readiness assessment and the dependency you flagged.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: Customer investment should be governed through the success plan, not treated as a separate administrative process.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints: Investment execution needs owners, milestones, handoffs, risk tracking and value evidence. The CSAM governs the operating rhythm and realization story.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions:
Is the investment on this account connected to the success plan, or running beside it?
Who owns delivery, and when did you last confirm status with them rather than assume it?
What evidence would the realization review need that you do not have yet?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one active or proposed customer investment, scope, milestone list or execution question.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions:
How does this investment show up in the success plan?
Which delivery status did you confirm rather than assume?
What evidence will the realization review need, and who is producing it?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for investment running as a parallel process rather than part of the success plan, delivery status inferred from silence, realization evidence identified only when the review is booked, and the CSAM answering eligibility or approval questions that belong elsewhere.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from the investment rhythm to the one checkpoint you will run this month and the evidence it produces.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If the tool or data source is unavailable, map the current workflow manually, name the trusted sources and draft the prompt plus human checkpoint for later testing.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name the investment checkpoint you will run, the delivery status you will confirm rather than assume, and the realization evidence you will start collecting.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Run one investment checkpoint and confirm a delivery status rather than assuming it.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the status you confirmed and how it differed from what you assumed.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: Today is about align partner and specialist support to technical priorities without turning the huddle into a tool demo or a status review.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints: The goal is A partner and specialist alignment plan with feature gaps, owners, timing, and next decision. AI can assemble evidence and draft options, but ATS judgment stays accountable for strategy, technical accuracy, and next decisions.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions:
Where is technical feature the constraint, rather than time or priority?
When you last brought in a specialist, did it change the outcome?
What would a partner need from you to arrive useful rather than catching up?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: confirm access to the named tools, bring one real account or technical strategy example, and review the commitment from the prior huddle.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions:
Is the gap feature, capacity, or clarity? They need different answers.
What exactly would you ask this partner or specialist to do?
What will you send them so they arrive useful rather than catching up?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for support requested by habit rather than by need, asks vague enough that anyone could decline them politely, briefings promised verbally and never sent, and customer-sensitive detail heading to an external partner without a classification step.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from the feature gap to one specific, dated ask with the briefing that makes it answerable.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If tooling is unavailable, map the workflow and human checkpoint manually, then draft the prompt for later testing.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name the feature gap, the specific ask you will send, who receives it, and whether that recipient is internal or external.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Write one specific partner or specialist ask and send the briefing that makes it answerable.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the ask, the briefing, and whether the recipient was internal or external.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: Investment requests slow down when inputs, owners, or open questions are hidden. Today is about readiness.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints: Separate facts from assumptions. Name confirmed inputs, gaps, contributors, policy/process questions, and next governed action.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions: Which request input is missing? Who owns it? What should not be represented as approved?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one live solution pursuit, solution play, lead list, opportunity, or investment case relevant to this huddle; confirm tool access; review last commitment and evidence.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions: What request input is missing? Who owns it? What decision must remain human?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for eligibility or funding implied rather than confirmed, hidden open questions, and contributor inputs without owners.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from request readiness to next governed action.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: Use a sanitized scenario if live investment data should not be used.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name the next governed investment action, owner, and evidence needed.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: Check one investment request against what a complete submission needs before you submit it.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring what was missing and where the request sits now.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: This huddle has no pre-written workflow. The team chooses one, which means the value depends entirely on picking a workflow people actually run. Anchor the session in real work and trusted context before anyone opens a tool.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints:
The workflow must be recurring, not a one-off.
Someone in the room must actually own it.
A specific recent example beats a general description.
If the team cannot name a real example, the workflow is too abstract to work on.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions:
What workflow are we improving today?
What triggers it, and how often does it run?
What inputs, constraints, and approvals shape it?
Whose work is it, and who else depends on the output?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Bring one recurring workflow you personally run and one recent example of it, including what made that run harder than it needed to be.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions:
Where in this workflow is effort or quality lost today?
What is the smallest step AI could assist, rather than the whole workflow?
What must a person verify before the output is used?
What would a one-week version of this experiment look like?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for scope that is too broad to test in a week, inputs the person cannot actually access, an output nobody would notice if it were wrong, and enthusiasm for a tool without a workflow behind it. Also listen for the opposite problem: a step so small that automating it changes nothing.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from the friction people named to one specific assistable step, then from that step to a single bounded experiment with an owner.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If a tool or data source is unavailable, map the workflow on paper and design the experiment for later execution. Use a hypothetical process shape if needed, but do not invent business facts, customer detail, or system behavior.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name the workflow you chose, the one step you will test, the human checkpoint you will keep, and the evidence you will bring back. If you cannot name an owner or a date, the experiment is not real yet; shrink it until it is.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: What will you test this week? State the input, the action, the output, who reviews it, and what would tell you to stop.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the actual output from your experiment, whether it worked or not. A failed experiment with evidence is more useful to the group than a success without it.

HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SessionIntroduction: Deal making features live inside Sales Agent. There is no separate agent to select: when you ask Sales a deal-related question, those features answer. This session is not about learning to run deals. It is about being able to find deal facts for your own accounts, whatever your role, instead of waiting for someone to send them to you.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.KeyTalkingPoints:
Deal Agent is a skill inside Sales Chat, reached by picking the Sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot. There is nothing separate to install or select.
Its primary motion is renewals, specifically EA and MCA-E. That is where it is strongest.
The trigger is specificity. A TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number returns real data; a vague account reference returns a generic answer.
Keep one chat thread per deal. Mixing several deals into one thread confuses the context and makes the history hard to audit.
Looking up deal facts is open to every role. Commercial decisions, approvals, and material amendments are not.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.DiscussionQuestions:
When did you last need agreement, licensing, or renewal information and have to ask someone for it?
How long did that take, and what did you do while waiting?
What have you assumed about a customer's entitlements that you have never actually verified?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.PreparationChecklist: Bring one real account you work on, and if you have it, an agreement number, enrollment number, or TPID. If you do not have an identifier, bring the account name and we will find one in the session.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FacilitatorQuestions:
What did the lookup return that you did not already know?
What did you previously assume about this customer's estate that turned out to be wrong or unverified?
Where does this stop being your call and become the deal owner's?
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ListenFor: Listen for vague prompts producing vague answers, which is the most common reason people conclude deal making does not work. Listen for a first response being treated as final on a complex deal, when the guidance is to re-run and verify against current data. Listen for several unrelated deals being worked in one chat thread. Listen for someone treating a retrieved figure as approved pricing or a commitment, or stepping past retrieval into structuring a deal that belongs to the AE or Commercial Executive. Also listen for the opposite: someone escalating a question they could now answer themselves.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.SuggestedTransitions: Move from the lookup you ran to the single fact that changes how you would open your next conversation with that customer.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.FallbackGuidance: If Sales Agent access is unavailable or a lookup returns nothing, work from an account you know and list what you would need to verify before the next customer conversation, then name who currently holds each answer. Do not guess at entitlements, pricing, or discount levels.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.WrapUpGuidance: Name the account you looked up, the one fact that surprised you, and one question you previously would have escalated but can now answer yourself. If nothing was new, pick a less familiar account before the next session.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.ReflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.CommitPrompt: What will you do this week? Look up one account before a real customer conversation and use one retrieved fact in that conversation.
HuddleFacilitatorGuides.BringBackEvidence: Bring the prompt you used, what came back, and whether it changed how the conversation went. If the lookup returned nothing useful, bring the prompt so the group can sharpen it.

HuddleAgents.Name: Sales Agent
HuddleAgents.ShortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
HuddleAgents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
HuddleAgents.WhenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
HuddleAgents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork.
HuddleAgents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean.
HuddleAgents.KeyBenefits: Brings sales data and actions into the flow of work. For renewals, work that previously meant gathering data from seven or eight portals over two to three weeks becomes a few natural language prompts, with the Deal Book assembled across more than a dozen source systems.

HuddleAgents.Name: ECIF Agent
HuddleAgents.ShortDescription: AI-powered experience layer, available through Sales Agent and Microsoft 365, that connects the systems used across the end-to-end ECIF journey.
HuddleAgents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Understand eligible investment offers; create compliant ECIF workscopes with guided, auto-populated inputs; identify suitable suppliers; submit requests; and track status, milestones, overdue actions, and delivery progress.
HuddleAgents.WhenToUseIt: Preparing or refining an ECIF funding request; selecting an eligible offer or supplier for an Opportunity and location; submitting a request; or tracking milestones and delivery across internal or partner-led projects.
HuddleAgents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not treat the agent as the final authority for policy, eligibility, compliance, funding approval, or supplier selection. Review generated content and required evidence before submission, and use governed ECIF channels for exceptions or approvals.
HuddleAgents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and select Sales from the left navigation. Start an ECIF conversation using one of the suggested prompts or the Prompt Gallery; include the Opportunity ID or customer name and a clear command such as list, give, or track. Review the generated workscope, supplier recommendation, or request status before taking the next governed action.
HuddleAgents.KeyBenefits: Reduces seller toil by bringing ECIF guidance and actions into one conversational flow; improves workscope completeness and first-pass quality; speeds the path from scope creation to IO/PO; and provides a connected view of requests, milestones, alerts, and delivery progress.

HuddleAgents.Name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
HuddleAgents.ShortDescription: AI assistant across Microsoft 365 apps and work data.
HuddleAgents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Draft, summarize, analyze, prepare, and create within familiar Microsoft 365 experiences.
HuddleAgents.WhenToUseIt: Everyday work grounded in emails, meetings, chats, files, and app content.
HuddleAgents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not use as a substitute for a specialized agent when the work requires a specific system or workflow.
HuddleAgents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot from the app launcher or copilot.cloud.microsoft and start in Chat.
HuddleAgents.KeyBenefits: Reduces time spent drafting, summarizing, and preparing work; uses permitted Microsoft 365 context to keep work grounded.

HuddleAgents.Name: Cowork
HuddleAgents.ShortDescription: Agentic Microsoft 365 experience for longer-running, outcome-focused, multi-source work.
HuddleAgents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Plans and executes multistep work, invokes skills, and creates deliverables with checkpoints.
HuddleAgents.WhenToUseIt: Complex tasks spanning Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 data, documents, presentations, and recommendations.
HuddleAgents.WhenNotToUseIt: Avoid for a quick single answer when Copilot Chat or a specialized agent is sufficient.
HuddleAgents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and select Cowork beside Chat. Describe the outcome you want rather than a single question, then review the work at each checkpoint it presents.
HuddleAgents.KeyBenefits: Executes multi-step work across Microsoft 365 instead of answering one question at a time. Built for delegation: it plans, invokes skills, works across data sources, and produces deliverables with review checkpoints.

HuddleAgents.Name: Scout
HuddleAgents.ShortDescription: Always-on agent designed to keep work moving across Microsoft 365 and the desktop.
HuddleAgents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Your AI desktop assistant for seller work. Prepare for customer meetings, summarize communications, organize actions, monitor priorities, and automate repetitive work across Microsoft 365 and sales systems.
HuddleAgents.WhenToUseIt: Continuous or proactive work that should persist beyond one chat.
HuddleAgents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not use it for a quick single answer that Copilot Chat would handle, and do not use it to bypass a human checkpoint just because it can run unattended. Anything it produces while running on its own still needs the same review as anything else.
HuddleAgents.StepsToGetStarted: Go to aka.ms/m, the internal Scout hub. Request the access package, complete the agreement, download and install Scout, then sign in with Microsoft 365 and GitHub as instructed. Start with a business outcome rather than a tool command.
HuddleAgents.KeyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

HuddleAgents.Name: Researcher
HuddleAgents.ShortDescription: Deep research agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot that produces structured, source-cited reports.
HuddleAgents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Combines work content and web research across multiple steps.
HuddleAgents.WhenToUseIt: Customer, market, competitor, industry, and strategic research requiring citations. Researcher is also reachable inside Sales Agent, which uses it to answer research questions; call Researcher directly when you want the full sourced report rather than an answer inside a sales conversation.
HuddleAgents.WhenNotToUseIt: Avoid for quick summaries or lightweight drafting.
HuddleAgents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and select the Researcher agent, then state the research question and sources.
HuddleAgents.KeyBenefits: Produces source-cited research reports rather than unattributed summaries, combining work content and web research across multiple steps so claims can be traced.

HuddleAgents.Name: Analyst
HuddleAgents.ShortDescription: Data-analysis agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot for statistics, trends, outliers, charts, and reports.
HuddleAgents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Analyzes supplied data and produces understandable findings and visuals.
HuddleAgents.WhenToUseIt: Multi-file quantitative analysis, trend analysis, and executive-ready data insights.
HuddleAgents.WhenNotToUseIt: Avoid when authoritative operational reporting must come directly from a certified business system.
HuddleAgents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and select the Analyst agent, then attach the data you want analysed.
HuddleAgents.KeyBenefits: Turns supplied data into findings and visuals a non-analyst can act on, including trends, outliers, and executive-ready charts, without building the analysis by hand.

HuddleAgents.Name: MSXI Assist V2
HuddleAgents.ShortDescription: Assistance within MSXI for report discovery, KPI definitions, and report actions.
HuddleAgents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Helps users find reports, understand KPI definitions, and take supported report actions.
HuddleAgents.WhenToUseIt: When the job is navigating MSXI content or understanding a metric.
HuddleAgents.WhenNotToUseIt: Keep separate from the in-report MSXI Copilot until product owners confirm convergence.
HuddleAgents.StepsToGetStarted: Open MSXI and select the robot icon in the top ribbon to launch the Assist pane. No enrollment is required.
HuddleAgents.KeyBenefits: Finds reports using natural language, explains KPI definitions in business terms, launches reports and applies filters, and detects issues with self-service resolution and one-click support escalation.

HuddleAgents.Name: Agent J.ai
HuddleAgents.ShortDescription: Text-based coaching experience grounded in Microsoft 365 context and curated content.
HuddleAgents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Helps users sharpen messages, rehearse conversations, anticipate objections, and plan next steps.
HuddleAgents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not use as the authoritative source for CRM or commercial data.
HuddleAgents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Agent J.ai in Microsoft 365 Copilot, then describe the conversation you want to rehearse and who you will be speaking to.
HuddleAgents.KeyBenefits: Rehearsal before the real conversation. Sharpens messages, surfaces objections you had not anticipated, and coaches on clarity and next step, grounded in Microsoft 365 context and curated content.

HuddleAgents.Name: Auto-Fix Pipeline Agent
HuddleAgents.ShortDescription: Agent in MSX intended to resolve supported pipeline hygiene issues.
HuddleAgents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Supports targeted pipeline cleanup inside MSX.
HuddleAgents.WhenToUseIt: When a Practice explicitly addresses supported pipeline hygiene correction.
HuddleAgents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not generalize beyond supported issues.
HuddleAgents.StepsToGetStarted: In MSX, open the Pipeline Hygiene workspace and select Auto-Fixes. Choose which automated fixes to enable, then review, accept, or revert the changes after they are applied.
HuddleAgents.KeyBenefits: One-click cleanup for supported pipeline hygiene violations, with review and revert available so the seller stays in control of what changes.
HuddleAgents.AccessUrl: Open MSX, then any account, then the Hygiene tab, then Auto-Fixes. No standalone URL is published.

HuddleAgents.Name: MSXI Copilot
HuddleAgents.ShortDescription: Copilot experience in MSXI reports for interpreting enabled business data.
HuddleAgents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Interpret enabled business metrics, report views, and signals in context.
HuddleAgents.WhenToUseIt: Use when the job starts from an enabled MSXI report or certified business signal.
HuddleAgents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not use as a replacement for human interpretation of KPI scope, report filters, or customer context.
HuddleAgents.StepsToGetStarted: Open an AI-certified MSXI report and use the embedded Copilot panel to ask questions about the metrics and trends in front of you. Availability varies by report.
HuddleAgents.KeyBenefits: Answers questions against certified report data without leaving the report. Explains what a metric means in the context of the filters and view currently applied.

HuddleAgents.Name: Customer Success Agent
HuddleAgents.ShortDescription: Teams-based customer success experience referenced in Customer Health Success Program dispatch guidance.
HuddleAgents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Supports Success Program dispatch and customer-success workflow steps where available.
HuddleAgents.WhenToUseIt: Customer Health Success Program dispatch or customer-success process steps that are explicitly supported.
HuddleAgents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not use as authority for policy, delivery commitments or customer-facing claims.
HuddleAgents.StepsToGetStarted: Confirm access, install the app in Teams if required, then follow the supported Customer Health Success Program dispatch workflow.
HuddleAgents.KeyBenefits: Connects Customer Health Success Program execution to CSAM workflow steps in Teams, so dispatch and follow-through happen where the team already works.
HuddleAgents.AccessUrl: Open the Customer Success Agent app in Teams. No published entry-point URL was located.

HuddleAgents.Name: MSX Deal Assistance
HuddleAgents.ShortDescription: The investment request front door inside MSX. Consolidates ECIF, ACO, Azure Access, and Solution Assessment requests that were previously spread across separate tools.
HuddleAgents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Create, submit, and track investment requests against an opportunity, with ROI calculation and opportunity data prepopulated rather than retyped.
HuddleAgents.WhenToUseIt: When an investment request needs to be created or submitted, or when you need the current status of one you already submitted.
HuddleAgents.WhenNotToUseIt: Not for building the workscope itself, which happens in ECIF Central, and not for policy or eligibility judgments, which stay with the accountable owner.
HuddleAgents.StepsToGetStarted: Open an MSX opportunity, go to the Deal Assistance tab, select New Request, then choose the request type such as ECIF, ACO, or Azure Access.
HuddleAgents.KeyBenefits: One front door instead of several legacy request tools. Opportunity data and ROI calculation carry over, so the request starts mostly complete.

HuddleAgents.Name: ECIF Central
HuddleAgents.ShortDescription: Where the workscope is built and where delivery actually runs, including supplier collaboration, milestones, and change requests.
HuddleAgents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Create a workscope against an opportunity, add suppliers and scope detail, calculate the spend plan, and track execution and milestones once funding is approved.
HuddleAgents.WhenToUseIt: When you need to build or revise a workscope, onboard or work with a supplier, or check delivery progress and milestones.
HuddleAgents.WhenNotToUseIt: Not the submission point. The completed workscope is submitted through MSX Deal Assistance.
HuddleAgents.StepsToGetStarted: Open ECIF Central, create a workscope using the MSX Opportunity ID, add suppliers and scope detail, calculate the spend plan, then generate the completed workscope for submission. Suppliers collaborate through partner.ecifcentral.microsoft.com.
HuddleAgents.KeyBenefits: Keeps workscope, supplier collaboration, and delivery tracking in one place instead of email threads and spreadsheets.

HuddleAgents.Name: Investment Tracker
HuddleAgents.ShortDescription: The status view inside MSX Deal Assistance showing where a request sits, who holds it, and what is blocking it. Sometimes called the Pizza Tracker.
HuddleAgents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: See request stage, current owner, blockers, and recommended next steps without asking someone for a status update.
HuddleAgents.WhenToUseIt: When a submitted request has gone quiet and you need to know where it is and who holds it.
HuddleAgents.WhenNotToUseIt: Not a substitute for contacting the owner when a request is genuinely stuck. It shows status, not urgency.
HuddleAgents.StepsToGetStarted: Open your submitted request in MSX Deal Assistance and review the tracker view for stage, ownership, and blockers. FY27 material describes proactive at-risk alerts; confirm current availability with the ECIF program team.
HuddleAgents.KeyBenefits: Replaces the status-chasing email with a view. Makes ownership visible so the next action has a name attached.
HuddleAgents.AccessUrl: Open the request in MSX Deal Assistance; the tracker is a view within it. No standalone URL is published.

HuddleAgents.Name: Azure Offer Navigator
HuddleAgents.ShortDescription: The front door for Azure investment offers, including Azure Accelerate, with eligibility guidance and nomination support.
HuddleAgents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Find which Azure offers an opportunity is eligible for, choose the right one, submit the nomination, and track its status.
HuddleAgents.WhenToUseIt: When the investment is Azure-specific and you need to identify and request the right offer.
HuddleAgents.WhenNotToUseIt: Not for non-Azure ECIF requests, which go through MSX Deal Assistance.
HuddleAgents.StepsToGetStarted: Open the Navigator, enter the MSX Opportunity ID, review the eligible offers it returns, select the appropriate one, and submit through the Navigator workflow.
HuddleAgents.KeyBenefits: One place to see what an opportunity actually qualifies for, with recommendations and next-best-action guidance rather than reading offer documentation.

HuddleAgents.Name: MCAPS Help for ECIF
HuddleAgents.ShortDescription: Support, guidance, and ticketing for ECIF and investment process questions.
HuddleAgents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Get help when a request is blocked, access is missing, or the process itself is unclear, and raise a case when self-help does not resolve it.
HuddleAgents.WhenToUseIt: When you are blocked on process, access, or tooling rather than on a business decision.
HuddleAgents.WhenNotToUseIt: Not for eligibility, policy, or funding decisions, which belong to the accountable owners rather than support.
HuddleAgents.StepsToGetStarted: Open MCAPS Help for ECIF, search the guidance first, and raise a case if the answer is not there. Have the opportunity ID and request ID ready.
HuddleAgents.KeyBenefits: A defined path for process and access problems, so a blocked request does not sit waiting on an informal ask.

HuddleAgents.Name: Consumption Manager
HuddleAgents.ShortDescription: Consumption plan information used inside Global ECIF and ACO request flows.
HuddleAgents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Supply and review the consumption plan detail that a Global ECIF or ACO request requires.
HuddleAgents.WhenToUseIt: When submitting a Global ECIF or ACO request that needs consumption plan information.
HuddleAgents.WhenNotToUseIt: Not a standalone consumption reporting tool. For consumption trends and ACR, use Sales Agent or MSXI.
HuddleAgents.StepsToGetStarted: Encountered as part of a Global ECIF or ACO submission rather than opened directly. Confirm current behavior with the ECIF program team.
HuddleAgents.KeyBenefits: Keeps consumption planning attached to the investment request rather than tracked separately.
HuddleAgents.AccessUrl: Reached within the Global ECIF and ACO request flow. No standalone URL was found in current documentation.

HuddleActivities.Name: Ask what the certified business data says
HuddleActivities.Description: Analyze aggregate pipeline position and gap drivers
HuddleActivities.Prompt: For the current quarter, where is pipeline most materially behind plan? Break the gap down by stage, solution area, expected close timing, and account. Identify the largest contributors, distinguish pipeline-volume issues from progression or timing issues, and show the metrics supporting each conclusion. Flag anything the available report cannot answer.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Enabled certified MSXI report; relevant report filters; current quarter scope
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Pipeline gap analysis by stage, solution area, timing, and account, with metrics and report limitations visible.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE confirms report, filters, KPI definitions, and interpretation before using the output in a forecast or management conversation.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Certified data creates a shared starting point for the judgment conversation.

HuddleActivities.Name: Find the right report and configure a useful view
HuddleActivities.Description: Report discovery, KPI clarification, filters, and bookmarks
HuddleActivities.Prompt: I need the best MSXI report for inspecting current-quarter pipeline gaps by account, stage, and solution area. Provide the report link, explain the relevant KPIs, and help me apply filters for [scope]. If supported, save a bookmark for this view.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Ask MSXI Assist for the best report for the question.
2. Confirm the KPI definitions match what you meant.
3. Apply filters for your scope.
4. Save a bookmark so the next inspection starts here.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Business question; role; scope; desired dimensions
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Report recommendation, KPI explanation, filtered view guidance, and bookmark or repeatable navigation path where supported.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE confirms report scope, definitions, and filters match the business question.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The right question in the wrong report creates confident noise.

HuddleActivities.Name: Review pipeline-hygiene corrections
HuddleActivities.Description: Review eligible automated or assisted pipeline-hygiene changes
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Open the Auto-Fix Pipeline Agent review queue in MSX.
2. Filter to your opportunities.
3. Review each suggested change against the real customer and deal timeline.
4. Confirm, adjust, revert or opt out on each item.
5. Note anything you reverted and why.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Eligible opportunities; current agent rule; seller permissions
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Reviewed pipeline corrections with accepted, adjusted, reverted, or deferred changes and rationale.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE remains accountable for record accuracy and validates each material correction against real customer and deal context.
