HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Automation can propose a fix, but the seller owns whether it represents reality.

HuddleActivities.Name: Receive pushed business-metric changes
HuddleActivities.Description: Subscribe to a relevant MSXI report or business topic
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Open Proactive Insights in MSXI.
2. Select the business topic or report you want monitored.
3. Set the scope and the cadence.
4. Save the subscription.
5. Review the first pushed summary and judge whether the signal is useful.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Available Proactive Insights topic or report; delivery preferences
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Proactive insight subscription with scoped signal, cadence, first pushed summary, and usefulness assessment.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE checks that the signal is useful rather than noisy and adjusts scope or cadence if needed.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Monitoring only helps if the signal is actionable and not another feed to ignore.

HuddleActivities.Name: Schedule account or opportunity checks
HuddleActivities.Description: Run a recurring MSX and interaction-grounded check
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Schedule this prompt for [cadence]: Review [scope] for opportunities with material changes, missing next steps, stale customer engagement, or newly surfaced risk. Show the source signal and one seller action for each item.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Open Sales Agent.
2. Enter the prompt.
3. Set the recurring cadence.
4. Confirm the MSX scope it runs against.
5. Review the first scheduled result before relying on it.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Connected MSX scope; cadence; seller access
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Scheduled MSX-grounded opportunity check with scope, cadence, source signals, and recommended seller actions.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE reviews the first scheduled result, validates source signals, and narrows scope if output is too broad.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Recurring checks should reduce review burden, not create another inbox.

HuddleActivities.Name: Pressure-test the forecast narrative
HuddleActivities.Description: Find the movement, risk or commitment in your forecast narrative that you cannot yet evidence.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review the forecast narrative. For each claim about movement, risk or commitment, state the certified source behind it and whether the judgment is yours or the data's. Identify the two claims most likely to be challenged in inspection and what evidence would settle them.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The forecast narrative; the certified data behind each claim; the commitments you have made to your manager.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A forecast challenge list separating sourced movement from seller judgment, with the evidence needed for the two weakest claims.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE confirms source accuracy, customer context, role ownership, commitments, and whether the risk changes the plan.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: If the decision path for Build a Decision-Ready Forecast Narrative is going to fail, it should fail here rather than in front of the customer.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the forecast follow-through plan
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn the forecast inspection into the specific actions and dates that change the position before the next review.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Turn the forecast narrative into a follow-through plan. For each at-risk commit and gap driver, define the action that would change it, the owner, the date it must move by, and the evidence you will check. Set the rhythm you will use to inspect it before the next forecast call.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The reviewed forecast narrative; the at-risk commits and their owners; the date of your next inspection.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A forecast follow-through plan with actions, owners, dates, evidence checks, and an inspection rhythm.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE confirms owners, due dates, customer commitments, and which actions require another role.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: You spend your time editing the follow-through plan for Build a Decision-Ready Forecast Narrative rather than staring at a blank version of it.

HuddleActivities.Name: Analyze certified forecast movement
HuddleActivities.Description: Analyze certified business metrics and drivers.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Give me my weekly forecast narrative for [scope]: qualified versus committed change since last week, the five biggest movers up and down with one-line reasons, committed deals at risk in the next 30 days, and three inspection questions. Use only the enabled certified report and show supporting metrics.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Your forecast scope; access to certified pipeline data; last week's position for comparison.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Forecast narrative with qualified versus committed movement, biggest movers, at-risk deals, inspection questions, and supporting metrics.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE validates source metrics, customer context, and whether the narrative reflects seller judgment.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A forecast narrative should make risk inspectable, not make uncertainty sound certain.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the inspection brief
HuddleActivities.Description: Synthesize approved analysis and work context into an artifact.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the approved forecast analysis and my meeting notes, draft a concise forecast-call brief that separates sourced facts, seller judgment, risks, decisions needed, and follow-up actions.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The approved forecast analysis; your own meeting notes; the risks you judge to be real but cannot yet evidence.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Forecast-call brief separating sourced facts, seller judgment, risks, decisions needed, and follow-up actions.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE reviews every claim, adds judgment, and decides what is shared with manager or leadership.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The brief turns analysis into a review-ready conversation.

HuddleActivities.Name: Pressure-test the account priority list
HuddleActivities.Description: Challenge whether your account priorities are driven by evidence or by habit and familiarity.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review my account priority list. For each of the top accounts, state the evidence behind the priority and whether it reflects a current signal or a standing assumption. Identify the account most likely to be wrongly prioritized, the account most likely to be wrongly ignored, and what would confirm either.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The prioritized account list; the source signal behind each priority; the accounts you have not touched recently.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A priority challenge showing evidence per account, plus the most likely over-prioritized and under-prioritized account.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE confirms source accuracy, customer context, role ownership, commitments, and whether the risk changes the plan.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: If the decision path for Prioritize Accounts and Build an Actionable Account Plan is going to fail, it should fail here rather than in front of the customer.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the account follow-through plan
HuddleActivities.Description: Convert the account priorities into named next actions and the rhythm that keeps them from decaying into a list.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Turn the account priority list into a follow-through plan. For each top account, define the next action, the owner, the date, the signal you will check to know it worked, and the point at which you would drop the account down the list. Set a weekly rhythm for reviewing it.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The prioritized account list; the next action for each top account; your weekly planning rhythm.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: An account follow-through plan with next actions, owners, dates, verification signals, and a weekly review rhythm.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE confirms owners, due dates, customer commitments, and which actions require another role.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: You spend your time editing the follow-through plan for Prioritize Accounts and Build an Actionable Account Plan rather than staring at a blank version of it.

HuddleActivities.Name: Assess ECIF fit and investment momentum
HuddleActivities.Description: Explore eligible investment options for an approved opportunity and identify request or delivery risks to momentum.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the approved opportunity ID or TPID, explore eligible investment offers, summarize customer investments, and identify request or delivery risks that could affect opportunity momentum. Separate retrieved facts from assumptions.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved opportunity ID or TPID and current opportunity context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Investment-fit summary with supported options, active-request status, risks, evidence gaps, and next human decision.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE confirms opportunity context and does not determine eligibility, approval, or funding. Route to the accountable ECIF owner.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Investment is useful only when it removes a real account or opportunity barrier.

HuddleActivities.Name: Prioritize account action for this week
HuddleActivities.Description: Use Sales Agent and available sales context to rank accounts and name one next action for each.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Rank my top 10 accounts for this week. For each, show the priority driver, active opportunity stage, renewal or whitespace signal, partner context, and the single highest-impact seller action. Show the source signal and flag missing context.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Your account list; access to opportunity, renewal and whitespace signals; partner coverage for those accounts.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Prioritized account list with priority driver, source signal, active stage, role gaps, and highest-impact action.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE validates the priority logic, relationship nuance, and whether the action is realistic this week.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Prioritization is a decision about what will not get attention.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build or assess the account plan with approval gates
HuddleActivities.Description: Use a reusable planning skill to propose account-plan updates while keeping every write or commitment AE-approved.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: For [Account] and [TPID], assess the current account plan, research evidence gaps, propose additive updates to priorities, stakeholders, opportunities, and next actions, and require approval before any MSX write.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Open Scout and start the account plan skill.
2. Supply the account and TPID.
3. Review the proposed additions against your own knowledge.
4. Approve or reject each proposed MSX write.
5. Confirm nothing was written without your approval.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The account and its TPID; the current account plan; your authority to approve or reject an MSX write.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Account-plan assessment with proposed updates, evidence gaps, and explicit approval/rejection decisions.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE approves or rejects each proposed change and confirms nothing is written or committed without review.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Account planning becomes usable when it creates next actions, not just more content.

HuddleActivities.Name: Pressure-test the opportunity hypotheses
HuddleActivities.Description: Separate the opportunity signals that are genuinely evidenced from the ones that reflect optimism.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review my opportunity hypotheses. For each, state the trigger event, the evidence it rests on, and whether a customer has actually indicated intent or the intent is inferred. Identify which would create duplicate or unsupported pipeline, and what one piece of evidence would qualify or kill each.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The opportunity hypotheses; the trigger and evidence behind each; your existing pipeline so you can spot duplication.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A qualification challenge per hypothesis, with evidence status, duplication risk, and the single test that would qualify or kill it.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE confirms source accuracy, customer context, role ownership, commitments, and whether the risk changes the plan.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: If the decision path for Create and Qualify New Opportunities is going to fail, it should fail here rather than in front of the customer.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the opportunity follow-through plan
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn qualified opportunity hypotheses into the first customer action and the date you will know whether it is real.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Turn the qualified opportunity hypotheses into a follow-through plan. For each, define the first customer action, the stakeholder, the date, the response that would confirm it is real, and the point at which you would stop pursuing it. Rank by which is most likely to convert.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The qualified hypotheses; the stakeholder you would approach for each; your outreach capacity this week.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A ranked opportunity follow-through plan with first actions, stakeholders, dates, confirming signals, and stop conditions.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE confirms owners, due dates, customer commitments, and which actions require another role.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: You spend your time editing the follow-through plan for Create and Qualify New Opportunities rather than staring at a blank version of it.

HuddleActivities.Name: Qualify buying signals into opportunity hypotheses
HuddleActivities.Description: Use Sales Agent and available customer context to separate real buying signals from noise or optimism.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review [Account] across MSX, recent meetings, email, and available content. Summarize buying signals, risks, existing opportunity overlap, and the top three actions to create or progress a qualified opportunity. Flag signals that lack evidence.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The account you are working; access to MSX, recent meetings and email for it; your open opportunities so you can spot overlap.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Buying-signal summary with evidence, risks, existing opportunity overlap, top actions, and unsupported signals flagged.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE verifies source access, customer intent, duplication risk, and whether the signal warrants outreach or opportunity creation.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A qualified opportunity starts with a trigger and evidence, not the need to fill coverage.

HuddleActivities.Name: Develop whitespace outreach from evidence
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn whitespace and account signals into testable outreach and first-meeting structure.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Analyze whitespace for [scope]. Identify accounts with low solution penetration relative to known priorities, propose the top three opportunity hypotheses, and create an initial outreach plan with a first-meeting agenda. Separate evidence from assumptions.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The territory or account scope; solution penetration data; the customer priorities you already know.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Whitespace opportunity hypotheses with evidence, assumptions, first outreach, partner consideration, and meeting agenda.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE validates account fit, customer relevance, partner appropriateness, and whether assumptions are acceptable for outreach.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Whitespace only matters when it becomes a customer problem worth testing.

HuddleActivities.Name: Inspect opportunity-level context before action
HuddleActivities.Description: Review connected MSX opportunities and available customer-conversation context
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review open opportunities closing this quarter for [seller or account scope]. Identify opportunities that need seller attention because the close date, next step, forecast evidence, or recent customer engagement appears incomplete or inconsistent. For each flagged opportunity, show the source signal, explain why attention may be needed, and suggest one seller action. Flag cases where recent customer context is missing.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Connected MSX scope; user access; seller or account scope
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Flagged opportunity list with close-date, next-step, engagement, and risk signals plus one seller action each.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE verifies the underlying records, customer context, and whether the proposed action is still current.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Opportunity inspection is where pipeline noise either becomes action or gets removed.

HuddleActivities.Name: Pressure-test the deal inspection
HuddleActivities.Description: Find the blocker, approval or stakeholder gap that the deal plan assumes is handled but nobody owns.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review this deal inspection. Identify the next decision the customer must make, whether the evidence to support it exists, and which blocker has no named owner. Name the assumption that, if wrong, would move the close date most, and what would confirm it.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The deal inspection brief; the exit criteria for the current stage; the account-team roles involved.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A deal challenge naming the next customer decision, unowned blockers, and the assumption with the largest close-date impact.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE confirms source accuracy, customer context, role ownership, commitments, and whether the risk changes the plan.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: If the decision path for Accelerate a Strategic Deal is going to fail, it should fail here rather than in front of the customer.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the deal follow-through plan
HuddleActivities.Description: Convert the deal inspection into owned actions and checkpoints that move the next customer decision.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Turn the deal inspection into a follow-through plan. For each blocker and open decision, define the action, the owner, the date, the customer-facing step if there is one, and the checkpoint where you will verify movement. Separate what you own from what the account team owns.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The reviewed deal inspection; the account-team owners; the customer decision date you are working toward.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A deal follow-through plan separating seller-owned from team-owned actions, with dates and verification checkpoints.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE confirms owners, due dates, customer commitments, and which actions require another role.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: You spend your time editing the follow-through plan for Accelerate a Strategic Deal rather than staring at a blank version of it.

HuddleActivities.Name: Inspect deal context before customer action
HuddleActivities.Description: Use the deal making features in Sales Agent to assemble agreement, enrollment, renewal, discount, and consumption context, then shape the deal from real data rather than recollection.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Show me the list of enrollments for [Account name or TPID], then list all agreements with type and status. For the agreement I name, provide license estate details grouped by SKU, list the SKUs whose discount is between 40 and 60 percent, and show the upcoming renewals with expiry dates. Lead with the identifier I give you. Tell me which figures you could not retrieve rather than estimating them, and flag anything that needs licensing or entitlement validation before I use it with the customer.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved account, TPID, enrollment, or agreement identifier and current deal context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A deal context brief covering enrollments, agreements, license estate by SKU, discount posture, and upcoming renewals, with retrieval gaps named.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE verifies the figures came from the source systems rather than inference, and routes pricing approval, policy exceptions, and final commercial authority to the accountable owner.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Deal making answers depend on the identifier. A named enrollment or agreement returns real deal data; a vague account reference returns a generic summary.

HuddleActivities.Name: Generate the Deal Book for a renewal and choose your scenario
HuddleActivities.Description: Compile the renewal summary for one agreement, then decide which pricing scenario to lead with and why.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Create Deal Book for agreement number [agreement number]. If the agreement number does not resolve, try the enrollment number instead. When it returns, summarize the pricing scenarios it produced, what each assumes about the customer, and what evidence in the purchase history and current licensing footprint supports each one. Tell me which scenario you would lead with for [customer context] and what would have to be true for that to be wrong. Flag any upsell or cross-sell recommendation that is not supported by the consumption data. Do not present a scenario as approved or as a commitment.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Have the agreement number ready; the enrollment number also works.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Review the Agreement Details sheet, including year-over-year revenue, before the scenario tabs.
4. Check the Reason to Believe tooltips on the List Price column for SKUs marked discontinued, new, or replaced.
5. Treat the first output as a draft; re-run if the data looks stale.
6. Decide which scenario to lead with and why.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: An agreement number or enrollment number for a real renewal. Customer context that would make one scenario more appropriate than another. Sales Agent access with your CRM scope connected.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A Deal Book with purchase history, current licensing footprint, pricing scenarios, and upsell or cross-sell recommendations, plus your reasoned choice of which scenario to lead with.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE validates the deal facts against the source data, decides which scenario fits this customer, and routes pricing approval, exceptions, and material amendments to the accountable owner and approval chain rather than acting on the recommendation alone.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The Deal Book assembles in minutes what used to take weeks across seven or eight portals. The judgment that matters is which scenario fits this customer.

HuddleActivities.Name: Prepare grounded customer follow-up
HuddleActivities.Description: Translate an approved inspection into grounded follow-up.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the reviewed deal inspection and latest customer interaction, draft a follow-up that confirms customer outcomes, open decisions, commitments, and the next agreed action. Do not invent commitments.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The reviewed deal inspection; notes from the latest customer interaction; the commitments already made to the customer.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Customer follow-up draft confirming outcomes, decisions, commitments, next action, and any open questions.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE validates tone, relationship context, commitments, and whether follow-up should be sent or revised.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A good follow-up turns inspection into customer momentum.

HuddleActivities.Name: Turn the chosen scenario into a quote and start the approval
HuddleActivities.Description: Create the EA quote from the scenario you selected, check the pricing fields, and request the approval you know it will need, rather than discovering the approval requirement later.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Create an EA Quote for [enrollment number] based on the scenario I selected from the Deal Book. Then show me the price settings so I can check them, and tell me which fields you populated from the Deal Book versus which need my input. Identify any discount level in this quote that will require approval, and what the approval path would be. Do not submit anything or represent any discount as approved. If a guardrail or validation issue applies to this deal, including anything multi-year or multi-tenant, surface it now rather than at submission.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Bring the enrollment number and the scenario you chose from the Deal Book.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Review the price settings and correct anything that came across wrong.
4. Note the approval that will be needed and who owns it.
5. If a discount needs approval, request it: Request approval for a [X percent] discount on this renewal.
6. Keep this in the same chat thread as the rest of this deal.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The enrollment number and the Deal Book scenario you selected. Knowledge of your own empowerment level and who owns approval beyond it. Sales Agent access with your CRM scope connected.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A draft EA quote with price settings visible, a clear split between populated and required fields, and the approval requirement and path named before submission.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE verifies every pricing field before submission, treats the draft as a draft rather than a final quote, and routes discount approval, exceptions, and any material amendment through the accountable owner and the legal approval chain rather than around it.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Deals stall between a good scenario and a submitted quote. Knowing the approval requirement before you build the quote is what keeps that gap short.

HuddleActivities.Name: Pressure-test the executive conversation plan
HuddleActivities.Description: Test the conversation plan against the objections and stakeholder dynamics most likely to derail it.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review my plan for this executive conversation. Identify the claim most likely to be challenged, the stakeholder most likely to resist, the evidence I am missing for my primary ask, and whether my fallback ask is genuinely different or just a smaller version of the same one.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The conversation brief; the stakeholder history and dynamics; the ask you intend to make.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A conversation challenge naming the weakest claim, the likely resistor, missing evidence, and fallback-ask quality.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE confirms source accuracy, customer context, role ownership, commitments, and whether the risk changes the plan.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: If the decision path for Prepare for a Customer Conversation is going to fail, it should fail here rather than in front of the customer.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build the account and conversation brief
HuddleActivities.Description: Use MSX and available customer-interaction context to prepare the AE.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Prepare me for my next conversation with [Account]. Summarize priorities from the last 60 days, sentiment shifts, open commitments, active MSX opportunities, competitive mentions, engaged account-team roles, and missing context. Recommend three talking points and the single ask that best advances the customer decision. Show the source signal for each major claim.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Account; meeting type; desired decision; user access to MSX and available customer context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Grounded AE conversation brief with source signals, gaps, talking points, likely objections, primary ask, and fallback ask.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE verifies customer facts, relationship nuance, opportunity strategy, claims, commitments, and the ask before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Preparation is the highest-leverage place to improve the customer conversation.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the executive value narrative
HuddleActivities.Description: Create a customer-ready narrative from approved evidence and work content.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the approved account brief and these source materials, create an executive value narrative for [solution/workload]. Map the solution to the customer’s stated priorities, use only sourced outcomes or quantified evidence, flag claims requiring review, and end with three CXO talking points, one primary ask, and one realistic fallback ask.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved account brief; selected files, meetings, or content; solution/workload; desired decision.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Executive value narrative with sourced claims, customer priorities, CXO talking points, primary ask, fallback ask, and review flags.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE and relevant technical or commercial roles validate all claims, ROI, customer commitments, and tone before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Value that is not evidenced is opinion; value that is not connected to an ask does not move the decision.

HuddleActivities.Name: Research the customer and competitive position with citations
HuddleActivities.Description: Build the sourced research base for the executive conversation, so claims can be traced back to something.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Act as my research analyst for an upcoming executive conversation with [Customer]. Produce a sourced brief covering their stated business priorities, recent public announcements and results, the industry pressures they are under, their current technology direction, and any competitor positioning that is likely to come up. Cite every claim. Separate what you found in published sources from what you found in our own work content, and state clearly where you found nothing rather than filling the gap.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Customer name; the executive and their remit; approved access to work content and public sources.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Sourced research brief with citations, separating published sources from internal work content, and naming the gaps.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE verifies each citation actually supports the claim, discards anything unsourced, and decides what is appropriate to reference in front of the customer.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: An executive notices the difference between a seller who did the research and one who read the account record. Researcher is also available inside Sales Agent, which draws on it to answer research questions; using it directly gives you the full sourced report and the citations.

HuddleActivities.Name: Pressure-test the renewal assessment
HuddleActivities.Description: Test whether your renewal risk read is supported by usage and engagement evidence or by the absence of bad news.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review my renewal assessment. For each at-risk renewal, state the evidence behind the risk rating, when the customer was last genuinely engaged, and whether the value delivered has been demonstrated or assumed. Identify the renewal where I am most likely to be wrong and why.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The renewal view with risk evidence; consumption and usage trends; recency of real customer engagement.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A renewal challenge with risk evidence, engagement recency, value-proof status, and the renewal most likely misjudged.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE confirms source accuracy, customer context, role ownership, commitments, and whether the risk changes the plan.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: If the decision path for Manage Renewal Risk and Expansion Readiness is going to fail, it should fail here rather than in front of the customer.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the renewal follow-through plan
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn the renewal read into the actions and dates that change the outcome while there is still runway.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Turn the renewal assessment into a follow-through plan. For each at-risk renewal, define the action, the owner, the date it must happen by given the renewal date, the value evidence to assemble, and the point at which CE or commercial support must be engaged.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The reviewed renewal view; the renewal dates and their lead times; the account-team and CE owners.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A renewal follow-through plan with actions, owners, deadline-aware dates, value evidence, and CE engagement triggers.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE confirms owners, due dates, customer commitments, and which actions require another role.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: You spend your time editing the follow-through plan for Manage Renewal Risk and Expansion Readiness rather than staring at a blank version of it.

HuddleActivities.Name: Assess renewal risk and expansion readiness
HuddleActivities.Description: Use Sales Agent and available customer context to prioritize upcoming renewals by risk and supported expansion signals.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Show my accounts with renewals in the next six months. For each, summarize ARR, licensing, consumption trend, usage gaps, recent customer engagement, expansion signals, and risk evidence. Prioritize by potential impact and flag missing data.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Your renewal portfolio for the next six months; licensing, consumption and usage data; recent customer engagement history.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Renewal risk view with ARR, licensing, consumption or usage trend, engagement recency, expansion signal, impact priority, and missing data.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE validates renewal facts, customer intent, value evidence, and owner alignment with CSAM, CSA, CE, and SSP.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Renewal risk found early is still actionable.

HuddleActivities.Name: Draft a renewal outreach package
HuddleActivities.Description: Synthesize reviewed evidence into customer communication.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: For [Account] renewing in [Month], use the reviewed renewal assessment and source materials to draft outreach tied to stated goals, value delivered, unresolved consumption gaps, and expansion options. Flag pricing or commercial claims for CE review.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The reviewed renewal assessment; the customer's stated goals; the value evidence you can support, and your CE contact for pricing claims.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Renewal outreach draft with customer goals, value delivered, consumption gaps, expansion options, and CE-review flags.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE validates customer claims, tone, commercial statements, and whether expansion is supported by evidence.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Renewal outreach should connect value and next action, not just announce a date.

HuddleActivities.Name: Assemble the renewal and expansion package
HuddleActivities.Description: Pull the renewal position, consumption evidence, value story and expansion options into one package the customer and the account team can both work from.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Build a renewal and expansion package for [Customer]. Work across the agreement and renewal position, consumption and usage evidence, the value delivered so far, open risks, and the expansion options we believe are supported. Produce a short customer-facing summary, an internal account-team view with the risks stated plainly, and a one-page value story. Show me the plan before you build it, and check in before each document so I can redirect you.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Bring the customer, the renewal date, and the value evidence you can actually support.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Separate what the package claims as delivered value from what is projected.
4. Flag every pricing or commercial statement for CE review before the package goes near the customer.
5. Confirm the expansion options are grounded in usage evidence rather than aspiration.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved renewal, consumption, usage and value evidence for the account; the expansion hypotheses already tested.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Renewal package with a customer-facing summary, an internal risk view, and a one-page value story.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE validates every claim in the customer-facing material, confirms commercial statements with the Commercial Executive, and decides what is shared externally.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The renewal conversation needs a package, not a chat answer. This is multistep work across several sources, with checkpoints, which is what Cowork is for.

HuddleActivities.Name: Identify where customer investment could unlock the next decision
HuddleActivities.Description: Identify where a customer investment could remove a decision, deployment or adoption barrier, without judging eligibility.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using approved account, opportunity, customer-priority, and adoption context, identify where a customer investment could remove a decision, deployment, or adoption barrier. Separate evidence from assumptions and do not determine eligibility or approval.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Customer priorities, opportunity context, adoption or deployment barrier
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Investment hypothesis with customer outcome, opportunity linkage, barrier evidence, assumptions, and next human decision.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE confirms the barrier is real, investment is a plausible lever, and eligibility or approval is not implied.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Naming where customer investment could unlock the next decision is most of the work. Unnamed problems never get an owner.

HuddleActivities.Name: Connect proposed investment to account strategy and outcomes
HuddleActivities.Description: Connect a proposed investment to account priorities and opportunity milestones, naming unsupported claims and dependencies.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Explain how the proposed investment supports account priorities, opportunity milestones, and intended customer outcomes. Identify unsupported claims, dependencies, and the owner of the next decision.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Proposed engagement, scope inputs, intended outcomes
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Account-level investment rationale with customer outcomes, opportunity milestones, dependencies, unsupported claims, and owner.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE validates account strategy fit, source evidence, and accountable decision owner before routing.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Making proposed investment to account strategy and outcomes explicit is the part almost nobody does, and the part that travels.

HuddleActivities.Name: Confirm account-team sponsorship and handoff
HuddleActivities.Description: Create the handoff showing investment purpose, contributors, unresolved questions and who is accountable next.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Create a concise handoff showing the investment purpose, approved customer context, contributors, unresolved questions, and the person accountable for progressing the request.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved context and current investment status
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Account sponsorship and handoff brief with purpose, contributors, unresolved questions, owner, and next governed action.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE confirms role ownership and does not bypass governed ECIF or investment process steps.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Confirming account-team sponsorship and handoff now costs a conversation. Discovering it late costs a decision.

HuddleActivities.Name: Qualify the investment before anyone builds a request
HuddleActivities.Description: Test whether the investment idea is worth the effort of a request, and decide who owns the next step, before work starts.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Here is the investment hypothesis for [account and opportunity]: [paste]. Test it. What customer outcome would it unlock that will not happen otherwise? What evidence supports that, and what is assumption? What would need to be true for this to be declined, and is any of that already true? If this is Azure-specific, note that Azure Offer Navigator is the front door rather than a general ECIF request. Recommend proceed, reshape, or stop, and say who owns the next step. Do not assess eligibility or approval likelihood.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Bring the investment hypothesis from the previous activity.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Be honest about which supporting points are assumption.
4. Decide proceed, reshape, or stop.
5. If proceeding, name who builds the request and who owns the workscope.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The investment hypothesis and its account linkage. What the customer has actually said. Who on the account team would build and own the request.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A proceed, reshape, or stop decision with the evidence and assumptions separated, and the owner of the next step named.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE owns the judgment about whether the customer outcome is real, and routes eligibility, policy, and funding questions to the accountable owners rather than answering them.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The cheapest investment request is the one you decide not to build. Qualifying early costs an hour; qualifying late costs the team weeks.

HuddleActivities.Name: Test whether customer investment would unblock this deal
HuddleActivities.Description: Check the deal for a barrier that customer investment could remove.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the approved opportunity, account priorities and current blockers, identify whether a customer investment could remove a decision, deployment or adoption barrier on this deal. Separate evidence from assumption. Do not determine eligibility, funding or approval.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved opportunity context, current blockers, account priorities
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Deal-linked investment hypothesis with barrier, evidence, assumptions, owner, and next human decision.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE confirms the barrier is real, investment is appropriate, and funding or eligibility remains a governed decision.
HuddleActivities.BestFitJob: Check the deal for a barrier that customer investment could remove.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Investment belongs in the deal conversation only when it changes a real blocker.

HuddleActivities.Name: Watch your accounts for buying signals worth acting on
HuddleActivities.Description: Set up a standing watch across your account list so external and internal signals reach you while they are still actionable.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Set up a recurring watch across my named accounts. Each week, surface publicly reported changes - leadership moves, earnings commentary, announced initiatives, regulatory or funding events - alongside internal signals such as new support volume, usage shifts, or newly opened engagements. For each signal, state what it plausibly implies for a Microsoft opportunity and what would have to be true for that to hold. Separate what is evidenced from what is inference, and cite the source for every external claim.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Bring your named account list and confirm which of those accounts you can see internal activity for.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Check the first digest against one account you know well, and confirm every external claim carries a source.
4. Set the cadence you will actually read; weekly is usually enough.
5. Discard any signal you cannot trace to a source before acting on it.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Your named account list; access to internal account activity; the priority solution areas for your territory.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A recurring signal digest per account with sourced external events, internal activity changes, and an explicit evidence-versus-inference split.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE validates each signal against what they know about the account before acting, and never repeats an unsourced claim to a customer.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Opportunity creation is mostly a timing problem. The trigger events that make an account ready are public or visible internally - the constraint is noticing them while there is still time to act.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build the account-team role and handoff map
HuddleActivities.Description: Clarify who needs to be involved, what input they owe, and which customer decision the team is supporting.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: For [Account or Opportunity], build an account-team role and handoff map. Include customer outcome, current stage, required Microsoft roles, partner role if relevant, missing coverage, owner for each action, input needed, due date, and the next customer decision. Flag unsupported assumptions and stale context.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Account or opportunity context; current stage; known team members; desired customer decision.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Account-team role and handoff map with missing roles, owners, inputs, dates, and next customer decision.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE validates role need, relationship nuance, owner accountability, partner fit, and customer commitments before sharing.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Most account-team friction is hidden until the handoff fails. Naming it early makes it manageable.

HuddleActivities.Name: Prepare partner co-sell engagement
HuddleActivities.Description: Identify where partner involvement could improve scale, specialization, credibility, or deal velocity.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Recommend whether partner engagement is useful for [Opportunity]. Identify candidate partner roles, evidence of fit from approved sources, dependencies, risks, proposed two-week ask, and a draft internal introduction. Do not imply partner acceptance or incentive eligibility unless confirmed by approved sources.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Opportunity; solution area; customer context; approved partner evidence or criteria.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Partner engagement recommendation with role, evidence, risks, dependencies, draft intro, and next ask.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE validates partner evidence, conflicts, ownership, customer fit, and any incentive or co-sell claims before outreach.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Partner engagement helps only when the partner role is specific enough to move the customer decision.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the account-team briefing and follow-through rhythm
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn context, role asks, and open decisions into a reusable team brief and follow-up rhythm.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Create a briefing for my extended account team ahead of [event or decision]. Include objective, customer context, open commitments, each role’s expected contribution, prep required, questions I need answered, and follow-up cadence. Keep it concise and flag claims needing validation.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Choose the account or opportunity.
2. Identify the decision or event.
3. Generate the brief.
4. Validate role asks and sensitive claims.
5. Send or store the brief and create follow-up owners.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Account context; event or decision; role list; open commitments; approved source materials.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Account-team briefing with role-specific asks, prep, open questions, and follow-through owners.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE confirms role asks, relationship sensitivities, source accuracy, and whether the brief should be shared.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A team brief reduces repeated context-setting and makes follow-through inspectable.

HuddleActivities.Name: Keep pipeline hygiene current between reviews
HuddleActivities.Description: Stand up a recurring sweep of your owned pipeline so hygiene problems surface on a schedule instead of the night before a review.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Check my owned pipeline on a recurring basis and report only what has changed since the last run. Flag opportunities with a close date in the past, no activity in the last 30 days, a missing or generic next step, or a stage that has not moved while the close date has. For each one, draft the specific update or question I would need to resolve it. Rank by revenue at risk within the current period. Do not change any record - produce a review list for me to action.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Confirm your team's definition of a healthy next step so the check flags the right things.
2. Run the prompt against your owned pipeline.
3. Review the first list and confirm each flagged opportunity is genuinely stale rather than deliberately paused.
4. Set the cadence to land before your pipeline review, not after it.
5. Make every record change yourself; do not let the check write to MSX.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Access to your owned pipeline; your current period close dates; your team's definition of a healthy next step.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A recurring change-only hygiene list ranked by revenue at risk, with a drafted resolution for each flagged opportunity.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE confirms each flagged item is genuinely stale before updating, and makes every record change themselves rather than delegating the write.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Pipeline hygiene fails because it is a periodic scramble rather than a standing habit. A recurring check that reports only what changed turns a two-hour clean-up into a five-minute review.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build the QBR and value evidence brief
HuddleActivities.Description: Assemble outcomes, commitments, usage or consumption signals, risks, investments, and expansion plays into a reviewable evidence base.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: For [Account] and [period], build a QBR evidence brief. Include outcomes delivered, supporting evidence, open customer and Microsoft commitments, usage or consumption signals, active investments, risks, expansion plays, and missing evidence. Separate sourced facts from interpretation.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Account; period; approved usage, consumption, meeting, opportunity, investment, and commitment sources.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: QBR evidence brief with supported outcomes, commitments, risks, expansion plays, and evidence gaps.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE validates source evidence, customer-recognized value, unsupported claims, and which roles must review.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A QBR should start with evidence the customer would recognize, not slides that sound good internally.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the executive QBR narrative and strategic asks
HuddleActivities.Description: Convert the reviewed evidence brief into an executive-ready narrative with decisions and asks.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the reviewed QBR evidence brief, create an executive QBR narrative for [Account]. Include a concise executive summary, value delivered, commitments, risks, top expansion plays, investment status if relevant, three strategic asks, and claims requiring final review.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Review the evidence brief.
2. Generate the QBR narrative or deck outline.
3. Remove unsupported claims.
4. Validate with account-team owners.
5. Decide what becomes customer-facing.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Reviewed QBR evidence brief; customer audience; desired decisions; approved branding or format constraints.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Executive QBR narrative or deck outline with value story, risks, expansion plays, and strategic asks.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE validates tone, customer relevance, commitments, claims, and whether technical or commercial owners must review.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The QBR should create the next decision, not just summarize the last quarter.

HuddleActivities.Name: Draft the executive value follow-up
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn reviewed value evidence and strategic asks into a concise customer-ready message.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Draft a follow-up email to [Customer Exec] using the reviewed QBR or value brief. Summarize the value supported by evidence, acknowledge open commitments, propose next steps aligned to strategic priorities, and include three talk-track bullets for my follow-up call. Flag any commercial or technical claims for review.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Reviewed value brief; customer executive; desired next step; approved source evidence.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Executive follow-up email and talk-track bullets with review flags.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE validates relationship tone, customer facts, commitments, and claims before sending.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Value is only useful if it reaches the right executive with a clear next step.

HuddleActivities.Name: Find out what this customer actually owns
HuddleActivities.Description: Retrieve the agreements, enrollments, and license estate for one of your own accounts, so you know what the customer already has before you talk to them.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: List all agreements for [Account name or TPID] with type and status, and show me the list of enrollments. For the agreement I name next, provide the license estate details grouped by SKU. Lead with the identifier I gave you. If you cannot retrieve something, say so rather than estimating it, and do not infer entitlements that are not in the data.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Bring one account you actually work on.
2. Run the prompt with the account name or TPID.
3. Pick one agreement from what comes back and ask for the license estate grouped by SKU.
4. Note anything you did not know.
5. Note anything you had assumed that turned out to be different.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: An account you work on, and ideally an agreement number, enrollment number, or TPID. Access to Sales Agent with your CRM scope connected.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A list of agreements and enrollments for the account, plus license estate grouped by SKU for one agreement.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: You confirm the retrieved data matches the account you meant, and treat entitlement and licensing detail as information to verify with the deal owner before making any customer-facing commitment.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Most roles walk into customer conversations without knowing what the customer already bought. The answer takes about ninety seconds to retrieve.

HuddleActivities.Name: See what is expiring and what that means for your work
HuddleActivities.Description: Surface upcoming renewals and consumption trend for your account, then work out what it changes for your own role rather than for the deal owner's.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: What are the upcoming renewals for [Account name or TPID]? Show expiry dates and current agreement details, then give me the ACR trend month over month for this account. Do not recommend a renewal strategy. I want the facts and the timing so I can work out what my own role needs to do before that date.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Run the prompt for your account.
2. Note the nearest expiry date.
3. Work backwards: what does your role need to have done before that date?
4. Name the one thing you would otherwise have found out too late.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The account and identifier from the previous activity. Your own role's commitments on that account.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Upcoming renewals with expiry dates, agreement detail, and consumption trend, plus one action your own role owns ahead of that date.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: You decide what the timing means for your own work, and leave renewal strategy, pricing, and commercial approach to the account owner and Commercial Executive.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A renewal date is a deadline for every role touching the account, not only for the person who owns the deal.

HuddleActivities.Name: Draw the line between what you can answer and what you should hand off
HuddleActivities.Description: Sort the deal questions you get asked into ones you can now answer yourself and ones that belong to the deal owner, so you stop escalating retrievable facts and stop answering commercial questions you should not.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Here are deal-related questions I have been asked recently by customers or colleagues: [paste the questions]. For each one, tell me whether it can be answered by retrieving facts from agreements, enrollments, licensing, or consumption data, or whether it requires a commercial, pricing, policy, or approval decision. For the retrievable ones, give me the prompt I would use. For the rest, say what kind of decision it is. Do not answer the commercial ones yourself.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. List the deal questions you have been asked in the last month.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Check the split against your own judgment.
4. Pick one question you used to escalate and commit to answering it yourself next time.
5. Pick one you should always route, and confirm who owns it.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Real questions you have been asked. Knowledge of who owns commercial decisions on your accounts.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Your questions sorted into retrievable and decision-requiring, with a prompt for the first group and an owner for the second.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: You own the judgment about where the line sits on your accounts, and confirm that anything commercial, pricing, policy, or approval related routes to the accountable owner rather than being answered from retrieved data.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Two failures cost time: escalating a question you could have answered, and answering one you should have escalated.

HuddleActivities.Name: Map the workflow the team chose and find where it leaks
HuddleActivities.Description: Make the chosen workflow visible end to end, then locate the specific steps where time, confidence, or quality is lost.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: I run this recurring workflow: [describe the workflow, what triggers it, how often, and who depends on the output]. Here is a recent example of it going badly: [describe what happened]. Break the workflow into its actual steps. For each step, identify what input it needs, what decision it requires, and who owns it. Then tell me which two or three steps most likely cost time or quality, and why you think so. Ask me for anything you need rather than assuming it. Do not propose tools yet.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Describe the workflow and one recent example.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Correct the step map where the model got your work wrong; that correction is where the learning is.
4. Agree as a group which step leaks the most.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: A recurring workflow you personally run; a recent concrete example; who owns each step; what inputs the workflow depends on.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A step-by-step map of the chosen workflow with the two or three highest-friction steps named.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: The person who owns the workflow confirms the step map matches how the work is really done, not how it is supposed to be done.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Most workflow friction is invisible to the person living with it, because they have already adapted to it.

HuddleActivities.Name: Design one bounded experiment you can finish this week
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn the highest-friction step into a test small enough to run before the next huddle and specific enough to judge.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Here is the workflow step I want to test: [paste the step and why it costs time or quality]. Design a one-week experiment. Specify: the exact input I will supply, the action I will take, the output I expect, who reviews it before it is used, what evidence I will bring back, and the stop condition that tells me to abandon it. Keep it small enough to run in under an hour total. If the step as described is too large to test in a week, tell me how to narrow it rather than proposing a bigger plan.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Take the step your group identified.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Cut the experiment down until it fits in an hour.
4. Name your reviewer and your stop condition out loud.
5. Put it in your calendar before you leave the huddle.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The friction step from the previous activity; what data or systems you can actually access this week; who could review the output.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A bounded experiment card with input, action, output, reviewer, evidence, and stop condition.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: You decide whether the experiment is genuinely small enough to finish, and you own the judgment about what output is safe to use in real work.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: An experiment that does not fit in a week does not get run, and an experiment without a stop condition never ends.

HuddleActivities.Name: Stress-test the workload readiness evidence
HuddleActivities.Description: Test each ranked workload for the readiness evidence that exists, what is still unproven, and who would need to confirm it.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review this workload prioritization. For each ranked workload, identify the readiness evidence that exists, the impact assumption being made, what is still unproven, the dependency most likely to block it, and the person who would need to confirm it.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Draft workload ranking, readiness signals, and approved account context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Workload readiness challenge list with unproven assumptions and named confirmation owners.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS confirms which assumptions must be validated before the ranking is allowed to influence technical strategy.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A ranking built on unproven readiness sends technical effort to the wrong workload.

HuddleActivities.Name: Package the workload decision brief
HuddleActivities.Description: Assemble the ranked workloads, rationale, blockers and validation steps into a brief the v-team can decide from.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the approved workload prioritization, create a decision brief with ranked workloads, rationale, owner, dependency, blocker, next validation step, and team ask.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved workload ranking and evidence.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Workload decision brief ready for team review.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS confirms priority, owner, dependency, and whether the team ask is realistic.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The priority is not real until the next action and owner are named.

HuddleActivities.Name: Validate technical and business assumptions
HuddleActivities.Description: Find the unsupported assumptions, unresolved risks and readiness gaps in a technical strategy before it is socialized.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review this technical strategy package. Identify unsupported assumptions, weak evidence, unresolved technical risks, customer readiness gaps, security or compliance dependencies, and decisions that require SME review.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Draft strategy package and source evidence.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Assumption and validation gap register.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS decides what to revise before sharing or acting.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: If the strategy is going to fail, it should fail here rather than in front of the customer.

HuddleActivities.Name: Validate briefing evidence and decisions
HuddleActivities.Description: Check that the briefing is designed to move a specific customer decision and that its claims and participants support that.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review this EBC plan. Identify the customer decision it is designed to move, evidence gaps, unsupported technical or business claims, missing participants, and follow-through risks.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Draft EBC plan and approved evidence.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Briefing validation checklist and fix list.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS confirms which fixes are required before the briefing plan is used.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A briefing plan without evidence and follow-through becomes calendar management.

HuddleActivities.Name: Brief the contributors so they arrive ready
HuddleActivities.Description: Give each contributor their objective, the evidence they own, the questions to expect and the time they have.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the validated EBC plan, create a per-contributor brief that states the session objective, what each participant must prepare, the evidence they own, the questions they should expect, and the time they have.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Validated EBC plan and confirmed participant list.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Per-contributor briefing pack with owned evidence and time allocation.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS confirms each ask is realistic and that no contributor is asked to present unvalidated evidence.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: An executive briefing fails quietly when contributors arrive unclear about their part.

HuddleActivities.Name: Define follow-through and inspection rhythm
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn briefing commitments into owners, checkpoint dates and the escalation triggers that keep them alive afterwards.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the approved EBC plan, create a follow-through plan with decisions, commitments, owners, evidence required, checkpoint dates, risks, and escalation triggers.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved EBC plan and participant list.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Follow-through and inspection plan.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS validates ownership, timing, and escalation boundaries.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The briefing creates value only if the next decision survives after the session.

HuddleActivities.Name: Find the weak claims before the customer does
HuddleActivities.Description: Audit the talk track claim by claim, separating what is evidenced from what rests on assumption or unshipped roadmap.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Audit this talk track claim by claim. For each claim, state the evidence that supports it, whether that evidence is approved for customer use, and what a technically informed customer would ask for. Flag any claim that rests on assumption, marketing language, or a roadmap item rather than something available today.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Draft talk track, current customer signals, and approved evidence.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Claim-by-claim audit separating supported claims, unsupported claims, and roadmap-dependent claims.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS decides which challenges are real and validates any technical claim before it is used with the customer.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Executive credibility is lost on one unsupported claim, and roadmap language is the most common source.

HuddleActivities.Name: Package the technical conversation brief
HuddleActivities.Description: Assemble the objective, signals, questions, objections and reviewed responses into one brief you can walk in with.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Package the approved talk track into a conversation brief with objective, audience, customer signals, opening, key questions, likely objections, reviewed responses, roles, and follow-up ownership.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved talk track and meeting context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Technical conversation brief.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS confirms claims, roles, and follow-up before sharing.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A talk track becomes useful when the team can align around it.

HuddleActivities.Name: Assess role coverage and handoffs
HuddleActivities.Description: Identify missing role coverage and handoff risk.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review [Account or Opportunity]. Identify current AE, ATS, SSP, SE, CE, CSA, CSAM, partner, and investment coverage for the technical decision in front of the customer. Flag missing roles, unclear owners, dependency risks, and the next handoff that needs confirmation.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Account or opportunity; current team context; decision to move.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Role coverage and handoff map.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS confirms who owns each input, action, and decision.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: You cannot orchestrate a team if the coverage gaps are invisible.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the technical CBR contribution
HuddleActivities.Description: Draft the ATS portion of a customer business review.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using approved account and technical sources, draft the technical contribution for a CBR. Include customer objectives, roadmap, technical progress, proof, risks, open decisions, asks, and follow-through owners.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved account, roadmap, proof, risk, and outcome sources.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Technical CBR contribution.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS validates technical accuracy, claims, proof, and customer relevance.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The CBR needs the technical story connected to customer outcomes.

HuddleActivities.Name: Review technical claims and evidence
HuddleActivities.Description: Check CBR technical content before sharing.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review this technical CBR contribution. Flag unsupported claims, missing evidence, unclear decisions, weak linkage to customer priorities, and follow-through gaps.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Draft technical CBR contribution and source evidence.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Claim and evidence review list.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS decides which claims to revise, remove, or route to SME review.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Unsupported technical claims weaken the whole customer review.

HuddleActivities.Name: Turn the hardest review questions into a readiness edit
HuddleActivities.Description: Find the three questions the content invites, then change the contribution so it answers them before they are asked.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Here is our technical contribution for a customer business review: [paste]. Identify the three hardest questions this content invites, including about progress that has been slower than planned and any risk we have named. For each question, state what evidence the content currently offers, whether that evidence is sufficient, and the specific edit to the contribution that would answer the question before it is asked. Return the edits as a numbered change list, not as a rewritten document. Do not treat a statement of intent as evidence.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Bring the reviewed CBR contribution.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Apply the edits where evidence exists.
4. For any question where evidence does not exist, decide whether to name the gap openly in the review or remove the claim.
5. Bring that decision to the huddle.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The technical CBR contribution; known risks and slow areas; who attends from the customer side; commitments made in prior reviews.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A numbered change list making the contribution answer its three hardest questions, plus any evidence gap named explicitly.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS decides whether to strengthen the evidence, name the gap openly, or remove the claim, and owns every technical statement made to the customer.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The credibility of a business review is decided by the answer to the uncomfortable question.

HuddleActivities.Name: Convert the review into technical decisions
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn what was discussed into the decisions, owners, and dates that make the next review shorter.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Here are the notes from the customer business review [paste]. Extract only the technical decisions that were actually made, the decisions that were deferred and why, and the ones that were avoided. For each open decision, state who needs to make it, what they need in order to make it, and by when it must happen to protect the roadmap. Do not record a decision as made if the notes show it was only discussed.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Capture review notes.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Separate made, deferred, and avoided.
4. Assign the top open decision an owner and date.
5. Confirm it with the customer.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Review notes; attendees; the roadmap and its dependencies; commitments made in prior reviews.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Separated lists of made, deferred, and avoided decisions, with owners and dates for the open ones.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS confirms which decisions were genuinely made and owns the follow-up commitments before they are shared.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A review that produces no decision guarantees the same conversation next quarter.

HuddleActivities.Name: Prioritize technical health risks
HuddleActivities.Description: Create a ranked technical risk response.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review available account, usage, deployment, support, and technical context. Identify the top technical health risks, evidence, impact, owner, intervention, and next checkpoint. Flag missing data.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Authorized account, usage, deployment, support, and technical context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Ranked technical risk response.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS validates risk significance, owner, and intervention.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A technical risk only matters when someone decides what to do about it.

HuddleActivities.Name: Coordinate the technical risk intervention
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn a reviewed risk into a coordinated action plan.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the reviewed technical risk response, create an intervention plan with owners, dependencies, customer communication needs, escalation triggers, and checkpoint dates.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Reviewed technical risk response and role context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Technical risk intervention plan.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS confirms owners, dependencies, and escalation path.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Risk response usually fails at the handoff, not the diagnosis.

HuddleActivities.Name: Raise the risk with the customer before it becomes news
HuddleActivities.Description: Draft the message that tells the customer about a technical risk early, in a way that keeps trust rather than spending it.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: We have identified this technical health risk: [paste risk, evidence, impact, and what we are doing]. Draft a short message to the customer technical owner that states the risk plainly, what we know and do not yet know, what we are already doing, what we need from them, and when we will update them next. Do not minimize the risk, do not over-apologize, and do not commit to a resolution date we have not agreed internally. Keep it under 150 words.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Bring the ranked risk and intervention plan.
2. Confirm internally what can be committed.
3. Run the prompt.
4. Adjust to your relationship with the customer.
5. Send, and diarize the next update.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The identified risk and its evidence; the intervention plan; what has been agreed internally; the customer relationship and prior communications.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A short, honest customer message with a named next update date.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS confirms no commitment is made that has not been agreed internally, and owns the decision to communicate and the wording.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A risk the customer hears about from us early costs far less than one they discover themselves.

HuddleActivities.Name: Find the risk the data does not show
HuddleActivities.Description: Test the health assessment against what people have said, not only against what the systems report.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Here is our current technical health assessment based on system data: [paste]. Here are recent notes and conversations with the customer team: [paste]. Identify concerns raised by people that do not appear in the system data, and any system signal that people are not talking about. For each mismatch, say which source is more likely to be right and what would confirm it. Do not treat silence as agreement.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Bring the data-based assessment.
2. Gather recent conversation notes. If dashboard or transcript access is unavailable, build a lightweight table by hand with source, date, owner, evidence, and your confidence in it, then use that instead.
3. Run the prompt.
4. Pick the mismatch that would hurt most if ignored.
5. Add it to the risk list or record why not.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: System-derived health assessment, or a hand-built substitute table if system access is unavailable; recent conversation notes with the customer team; who has been quiet and who has been raising concerns.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A list of mismatches between reported data and human signals, with what would confirm each.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS judges which human signal is credible and owns the decision to add or dismiss a risk.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The risks that damage accounts are usually mentioned in conversation long before they appear in a dashboard.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build a standing account intelligence hub the v-team can use
HuddleActivities.Description: Consolidate the scattered sources behind account planning into one maintained hub that refreshes rather than being rebuilt each planning cycle.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Build me a standing account intelligence hub for this account. Pull together the business context, current opportunities, stakeholder map, installed estate and licensing position, recent engagement history, and open risks into one structured place. Then keep it current on a recurring basis and tell me specifically what changed since the last refresh. Where a source is unavailable to you, list it as a gap rather than filling it with inference.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Confirm which account planning sources you can reach, and name the ones you cannot.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Review the first hub build against what you already know about the account.
4. Check that nothing customer-confidential has been placed where the wider v-team should not see it.
5. Set the refresh cadence and agree with the v-team who reads the change summary.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The account name; access to your account planning sources; the v-team members who need visibility.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A maintained account intelligence hub with a change summary each refresh and an explicit list of unavailable sources.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS reviews the hub for accuracy before sharing with the v-team, and confirms that no customer-confidential material has been placed where it should not sit.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Account planning quality is usually limited by assembly time, not thinking time. When the assembly is standing and self-refreshing, the v-team spends its hour on the judgement instead of the gathering.
