Include renewal context, consumption or usage trajectory, MACC or commitment risk if applicable, adoption gaps, value evidence, support or health risks, stakeholder health, expansion hypothesis and recommended v-team next action. Flag unavailable data.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Renewal context, agreements, consumption or usage signals, adoption data, value proof, health risks and stakeholder context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Renewal and growth readiness view.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSAM aligns with AE and validates which signals are appropriate to share or escalate.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Renewal risk is easier to change when it is seen through health and value before the renewal date.

HuddleActivities.Name: Prepare the AE and v-team alignment brief
HuddleActivities.Description: Create a brief that helps AE, CSA, SSP and CE align on renewal risk and growth actions.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Prepare a v-team alignment brief for [Account] renewal or growth readiness. Include the customer value proof, top risk, consumption or adoption gap, expansion hypothesis, roles needed, decision owner and 30-day action plan.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Renewal readiness view, v-team roles and next review context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: V-team renewal and growth alignment brief.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSAM confirms ownership boundaries and aligns with AE before external use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: CSAMs influence renewal outcomes by making value, risk and next actions visible to the account team.

HuddleActivities.Name: Validate the success-plan evidence
HuddleActivities.Description: Label every statement in the success plan as sourced fact, assumption or recommendation, and flag what is not customer-ready.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review the success-plan update and label each statement as sourced fact, assumption, recommendation or missing evidence. Flag anything that should not be shared with the customer yet.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Draft success-plan update and source material.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Evidence validation matrix for the success-plan update.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSAM removes unsupported claims and confirms customer-safe language.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Validation prevents the plan from sounding confident where the evidence is thin.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the CSDR-ready success-plan narrative
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn the validated success plan into a short review narrative covering progress, value, risk and the decision needed.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Turn this validated success-plan update into a concise CSDR narrative. Include progress, value, risk, decision needed and next action. Keep it customer-safe and avoid unsupported claims.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Validated success-plan update and CSDR audience context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: CSDR-ready success-plan narrative.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSAM validates tone, customer context and decision ask before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A plan matters more when the customer can understand the progress and decision needed.

HuddleActivities.Name: Draft the outcome-anchored success-plan view
HuddleActivities.Description: Draft or refresh the CSP around customer outcomes, milestones, owners, risks and review points.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using approved customer priorities, recent meetings, CSP notes and delivery updates for [Account], draft a Customer Success Plan view. Include outcome, success measure, milestone, owner, dependency, risk, next customer review point and evidence source. Separate sourced facts from suggested updates.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Customer priorities, existing CSP or notes, recent customer meetings, delivery milestones and known risks.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Outcome-anchored success-plan view with gaps and suggested updates.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSAM validates customer priority, owner, commitment, measure and source before updating any system of record.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Most success-plan toil is assembling scattered signals. The CSAM should spend judgment on the outcome and commitment.

HuddleActivities.Name: Inspect the plan for drift and missing accountability
HuddleActivities.Description: Find stale milestones, missing owners and risks that are not tied to action.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review this success plan for drift. Identify stale milestones, missing owners, unsupported outcomes, risks without mitigation, dependencies without dates and actions that no longer map to the customer priority. Recommend the smallest set of updates needed before the next CSDR.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Current success plan, action log, CSDR notes, milestone status and RAID items.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Plan-drift inspection with recommended updates.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSAM confirms what should be changed, retired, escalated or kept as-is.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A stale plan creates false confidence. Drift detection keeps the plan governable.

HuddleActivities.Name: Keep success plan commitments visible between check-ins
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn the success plan from a document reviewed monthly into a tracked set of commitments with standing visibility on what is slipping.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Track the commitments in this account's success plan on a recurring basis. For each milestone, tell me whether there is recent evidence of progress, whether the named owner has been active on it, and whether the date is still credible given what has happened since it was set. Flag anything with no evidence of movement and draft the specific question I should ask the owner. Report only changes and exceptions - do not restate the whole plan each time.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Bring the current success plan with milestones, owners and dates.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Review the exceptions list, remembering that no evidence of movement is not proof that nothing moved.
4. Set the cadence to run before your customer check-in.
5. Ask the named owner the drafted question directly rather than escalating first.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The current success plan with milestones, owners and dates; access to the engagement activity behind it.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A recurring exceptions-only commitment tracker with an evidence check per milestone and a drafted question for each stalled item.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSAM confirms the credibility judgement on each date personally before raising it, since absence of visible evidence is not proof of absence of progress.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Success plans decay quietly. The milestone that slipped is rarely announced - it is simply never mentioned again until the review.

HuddleActivities.Name: Draft the sponsor value update
HuddleActivities.Description: Summarize adoption progress and value evidence for a sponsor in their language, not in internal metrics.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Draft a sponsor update for [stakeholder] that summarizes adoption progress, value evidence, remaining gap and the next action needed. Use customer language and avoid internal metrics unless they support the outcome.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Validated value realization brief and sponsor context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Sponsor value update draft.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSAM validates evidence, tone, sensitivity and next ask before sending.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Sponsors need a clear value narrative, not a dashboard dump.

HuddleActivities.Name: Convert value gaps into next-best actions
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn adoption and value gaps into next-best actions with paired customer and Microsoft owners and a review date.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review the adoption and value gaps for [Account]. Recommend next-best actions, including customer owner, Microsoft owner, Success Program or delivery resource if relevant, expected outcome and review date.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Adoption gaps, value evidence, success plan and available delivery or program options.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Next-best-action list for value acceleration.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSAM validates fit, ownership and whether recommendations should enter the success plan.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The value story should lead to action, not just a better deck.

HuddleActivities.Name: Identify adoption friction and next activation actions
HuddleActivities.Description: Map usage gaps to customer priorities and build a short activation plan.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: For [Account and workload], compare current adoption or usage signals with customer priorities and licensed or committed scope. Identify the top adoption friction points, likely root cause, stakeholder owner and a 4-week activation plan with measurable milestones.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Usage or adoption data, customer priorities, workload scope, stakeholder context and prior adoption actions.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Adoption friction analysis and 4-week activation plan.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSAM validates whether the adoption action is relevant to the customer priority and achievable with available owners.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Adoption work matters when it changes customer behavior tied to a business outcome.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build the value realization brief
HuddleActivities.Description: Translate adoption, usage, delivery and outcome evidence into a customer-recognized value story.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Build a value realization brief for [Account]. Show what changed, what evidence supports it, how it maps to the customer outcome, remaining gaps and the recommended next action. Separate measured evidence from narrative interpretation.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Adoption data, usage signals, customer outcome, delivery milestones, support or health improvements and prior review notes.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Value realization brief with evidence and gaps.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSAM validates customer-recognized value, removes unsupported claims and aligns tone to the audience.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Value that is not evidenced is an opinion. Value that is not communicated is invisible.

HuddleActivities.Name: Track delivered value against what was promised
HuddleActivities.Description: Keep a running comparison between the outcomes committed in the business case and what consumption and usage data actually show.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Set up a recurring comparison between the outcomes we committed to in this account's business case and what the consumption and usage data now shows. Report the direction of travel for each committed outcome, flag any where the trend will not reach the commitment on the current trajectory, and state what evidence would be needed to make the value claim defensible to the customer's finance function. Distinguish measured results from projected results everywhere.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Bring the agreed business case, its committed outcomes, and the baseline used at commitment.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Confirm the tracker distinguishes measured results from projected ones on every outcome.
4. Check that the measurement basis has not changed since the commitment was made.
5. Verify any figure yourself before it is shown to the customer as delivered value.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The agreed business case and its committed outcomes; current consumption and usage data; the baseline used at commitment.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A recurring value tracker per committed outcome, showing measured versus projected, trajectory against commitment, and the evidence gap.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSA verifies the measurement basis has not changed and confirms every figure before it is shown to the customer as a delivered result.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Value claims lose credibility the moment a customer's finance function finds the number is projected rather than measured. Tracking continuously is what makes the claim survive scrutiny.

HuddleActivities.Name: Map evidence gaps against decision criteria
HuddleActivities.Description: Test each decision criterion in the discovery brief against the evidence you actually hold, so the gaps are visible before the customer finds them.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the discovery brief, map each proposed decision criterion to supporting evidence, missing evidence, assumptions, and required reviewer input.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The discovery brief with its proposed decision criteria; the evidence you currently hold for each; the reviewers who could close a gap.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Evidence-gap map tied to customer decision criteria.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: Confirm source accuracy, role ownership, customer context, policy or technical constraints, commitments, and any system action before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The gap map shows what must be proven before architecture, demo, or PoC work proceeds.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the discovery handoff package
HuddleActivities.Description: Package the bounded problem, agreed criteria, evidence gaps and owners so the next technical stage starts without repeating discovery.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Package the bounded problem, agreed criteria, evidence gaps, assumptions, owners, and next technical action for the account team.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The completed discovery brief; the agreed decision criteria; the named owner for each open item.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Discovery handoff package for the next technical stage.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: Confirm source accuracy, role ownership, customer context, policy or technical constraints, commitments, and any system action before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A clear handoff prevents discovery findings from being lost before design or proof work begins.

HuddleActivities.Name: Validate the technical scope for ECIF
HuddleActivities.Description: Review a proposed investment-funded technical scope for missing evidence and corrections before it reaches request review.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review the proposed ECIF technical scope, milestones, deliverables, dependencies, and acceptance criteria. Identify missing technical evidence and corrections needed before request review.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Draft workscope, architecture context, technical dependencies, and acceptance criteria.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Technical-scope review with issues, proposed corrections, and handoff notes.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SE validates technical content only and confirms that eligibility, policy, commercial, and approval decisions remain with accountable owners.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Confirming the technical scope for ECIF now costs a conversation. Discovering it late costs a decision.

HuddleActivities.Name: Validate architecture evidence and assumptions
HuddleActivities.Description: Find the unsupported claims and open security or operations questions in an architecture decision record before it is shared.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review the architecture decision record and source evidence. Identify unsupported claims, assumptions, security or operations questions, and reviewer needs.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The architecture decision record; the source evidence behind each option; the security and operations reviewers available to you.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Architecture evidence and assumption review.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: Confirm source accuracy, role ownership, customer context, policy or technical constraints, commitments, and any system action before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Architecture confidence improves when unsupported claims are visible before customer use.

HuddleActivities.Name: Package the architecture handoff
HuddleActivities.Description: Assemble the recommendation, criteria, dependencies and unresolved questions so the next technical stage can act on the decision.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Package the architecture recommendation, decision criteria, dependencies, validation steps, risks, owners, and unresolved questions for the next technical stage.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The validated architecture decision record; the named owner for each dependency; the next technical stage and who leads it.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Architecture handoff package.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: Confirm source accuracy, role ownership, customer context, policy or technical constraints, commitments, and any system action before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A clean handoff prevents design intent from changing silently during demo, PoC, or delivery.

HuddleActivities.Name: Validate demo evidence and known limitations
HuddleActivities.Description: Check what the demo actually proves, what it cannot, and which environment or permission constraints could break it on the day.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review the demo or workshop plan for evidence, known limitations, environment needs, permission constraints, and unsupported claims.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The demo or workshop plan; the environment and tenant it will run in; the claims you intend to make live.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Demo evidence and limitation review.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: Confirm source accuracy, role ownership, customer context, policy or technical constraints, commitments, and any system action before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The strongest demo is honest about what it proves and what still needs validation.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the demo follow-up and decision package
HuddleActivities.Description: Capture what the customer reacted to, what stayed unresolved, and the technical decision the demo was meant to move.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Package the demo outcome, customer reactions, unresolved questions, evidence shown, follow-up owners, and next technical decision.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The demo plan as delivered; your notes on customer reactions and questions; the decision the demo was designed to advance.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Demo follow-up and decision package.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: Confirm source accuracy, role ownership, customer context, policy or technical constraints, commitments, and any system action before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Follow-up turns the demo from an event into a decision step.

HuddleActivities.Name: Validate PoC success and exit criteria
HuddleActivities.Description: Test whether the PoC has measurable success criteria and a real exit condition, or whether it will quietly become a project.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review the PoC plan for measurable success criteria, exit conditions, dependencies, security or data assumptions, milestones, and owner clarity.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The PoC plan with its stated criteria; the data and environment assumptions; the owner of the exit decision.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: PoC criteria and readiness review.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: Confirm source accuracy, role ownership, customer context, policy or technical constraints, commitments, and any system action before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Measurable success and exit criteria prevent the PoC from becoming open-ended work.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the PoC decision and handoff package
HuddleActivities.Description: Package the hypothesis, criteria, exit decision and dependencies so the PoC result can be acted on rather than debated.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Package the PoC hypothesis, scope, success criteria, exit decision, milestones, dependencies, owners, and handoff requirements.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The reviewed PoC plan; the milestone owners; the team receiving the result if it succeeds.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: PoC decision and handoff package.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: Confirm source accuracy, role ownership, customer context, policy or technical constraints, commitments, and any system action before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A PoC handoff makes the final decision and next stage inspectable.

HuddleActivities.Name: Route unsupported technical answers for review
HuddleActivities.Description: Separate the answers that are supported from those needing an SME, policy owner or security reviewer, and name who decides each one.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review the answer matrix and create an exception list for unsupported, low-confidence, policy-sensitive, security-sensitive, or SME-needed items. Assign suggested reviewers and required decisions.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The completed answer matrix with confidence levels; your reviewer and SME contacts; the response deadline.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Exception and reviewer-routing list.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: Confirm source accuracy, role ownership, customer context, policy or technical constraints, commitments, and any system action before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Showing uncertainty early is better than discovering it after the response is distributed.

HuddleActivities.Name: Prepare the response quality checklist
HuddleActivities.Description: Build the final pass that catches unsourced claims, unapproved commitments and unresolved items before a technical response leaves the building.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Create a final response quality checklist covering source completeness, claim review, assumptions, approvals, unresolved items, customer commitments, and distribution readiness.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The near-final response package; the approvals already obtained; the customer commitments it implies.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Technical response quality checklist.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: Confirm source accuracy, role ownership, customer context, policy or technical constraints, commitments, and any system action before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The checklist protects the SE from sending a fluent answer that still lacks approval or evidence.

HuddleActivities.Name: Validate the blocker evidence and mitigation path
HuddleActivities.Description: Check that every blocker in the technical risk plan has evidence, an owner, a mitigation and a next decision rather than just a name.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review the technical risk plan and identify whether each blocker has evidence, impact, owner, mitigation, checkpoint, and a clear next decision.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The technical risk plan with its listed blockers; the evidence behind each; the owners you can realistically assign.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Blocker evidence and mitigation review.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: Confirm source accuracy, role ownership, customer context, policy or technical constraints, commitments, and any system action before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A blocker without evidence and owner remains an observation, not a plan.

HuddleActivities.Name: Prepare the delivery or account-team handoff for technical risk
HuddleActivities.Description: Package the technical risk, mitigation and re-engagement triggers so the account or delivery team can carry it without you in the room.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Package the technical risk, evidence, mitigation, owners, dependencies, re-engagement triggers, and handoff requirements for the account team or delivery roles.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The reviewed technical risk plan; the mitigation owners; the delivery or account-team roles receiving the handoff.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Technical risk handoff package.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: Confirm source accuracy, role ownership, customer context, policy or technical constraints, commitments, and any system action before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A clear handoff prevents technical risk from being rediscovered after the deal progresses.

HuddleActivities.Name: Sanitize and validate the reusable asset
HuddleActivities.Description: Check a technical asset for sensitive content, accuracy and missing prerequisites before anyone else reuses it.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review the asset for sensitive content, technical accuracy, prerequisites, limitations, permissions, owner, and validation checks before reuse.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The draft asset; the customer context it was built from; your team's rules on what may be shared internally.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Asset readiness and sanitization review.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: Confirm source accuracy, role ownership, customer context, policy or technical constraints, commitments, and any system action before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Reusable assets create risk when sensitive content or unvalidated assumptions travel with them.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the reuse note and repository metadata
HuddleActivities.Description: Write the tags, purpose, prerequisites and limitations another SE needs to find the asset and know whether it fits their situation.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Create the reuse note, tags, owner, purpose, prerequisites, example use, limitations, and repository metadata needed for another SE to find and adapt the asset.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The sanitized asset; where it will be stored; the owner who will maintain it.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Reuse note and repository metadata.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: Confirm source accuracy, role ownership, customer context, policy or technical constraints, commitments, and any system action before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Findability and context are what turn a useful file into a reusable asset.

HuddleActivities.Name: Monitor technical blockers across your accounts between reviews
HuddleActivities.Description: Set up a standing watch on the technical signals that predict a stalled deployment, so intervention happens before the review rather than at it.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Set up a recurring check across the accounts I support. Surface where deployment or consumption has flattened or declined, where a technical blocker has been open longer than expected, where a support pattern suggests an unresolved architectural issue, and where a planned milestone has slipped without a new date. For each, state the technical hypothesis and the evidence behind it, and name what you would need to confirm it. Do not diagnose root cause with confidence you do not have.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Confirm which deployment, consumption and support signals you can reach for the accounts you support.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Review each technical hypothesis and check the evidence actually supports it.
4. Set the cadence to land before your account or delivery review.
5. Confirm any blocker technically yourself before raising it with the customer.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The accounts you support; access to deployment, consumption and support signals; the committed technical milestones.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A recurring technical risk list with a stated hypothesis, supporting evidence, and the confirmation step for each item.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SE validates each hypothesis technically before raising it with the customer or the account team, and corrects any signal that reflects a known planned change.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Technical blockers are cheapest to fix early and most expensive to fix at a review. The signal is usually present weeks before anyone names the problem.

HuddleActivities.Name: Define the investment-funded technical scope and decision criteria
HuddleActivities.Description: Bound what the investment is technically meant to prove, including the assumptions, dependencies and explicit out-of-scope items.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Clarify the technical problem, bounded scope, architecture assumptions, decision criteria, dependencies, risks, and out-of-scope items that the proposed investment should address. Do not infer eligibility or approval.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Customer problem, opportunity context, proposed investment
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Bounded technical scope and decision-criteria brief.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SE validates technical content and confirms that eligibility, policy, commercial, funding, and approval decisions remain with accountable owners.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Clear technical scope prevents investment-funded work from expanding beyond the proof it was meant to produce.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the technical evidence and success-measure package
HuddleActivities.Description: Define the proof, milestones and observable success measures that let a reviewer judge whether the funded work delivered.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Identify the technical proof, readiness evidence, milestones, observable success measures, failure indicators, and review gates needed to evaluate the investment-funded work.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Draft scope and technical context
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Technical evidence and success-measure package.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: Confirm source accuracy, current policy and process, role ownership, decision authority, customer context, and any system action before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Observable success measures make the investment reviewable instead of anecdotal.

HuddleActivities.Name: Pressure-test investment scope against failure modes
HuddleActivities.Description: Stress the proposed technical scope for the assumptions and failure modes that would undermine the investment.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the draft technical scope and architecture assumptions, identify the assumptions that would most damage the outcome if wrong, the failure modes that would surface during delivery, and the evidence that would confirm or rule out each one.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Draft technical scope, architecture assumptions, known constraints
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Ranked assumption and failure-mode register with the evidence needed to close each one.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: Confirm the grounding sources, separate evidence from assumption, and validate the named owner and next decision before this reaches a customer or an approver.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Failure modes found during scoping are cheaper than failure modes found during delivery.

HuddleActivities.Name: Prepare the technical handoff to delivery
HuddleActivities.Description: Package the technical scope, evidence and success measures for the roles who will deliver against them.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the approved technical scope, evidence package and success measures, prepare a handoff for the delivery roles. State what is decided, what remains open, and which technical decisions must not change without returning to you.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved scope, technical evidence package, success measures
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Delivery handoff with decided items, open questions and re-engagement triggers.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: Confirm the grounding sources, separate evidence from assumption, and validate the named owner and next decision before this reaches a customer or an approver.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A handoff protects the technical decisions that should not change without re-engaging the SE.

HuddleActivities.Name: Define what an investment-funded proof must demonstrate
HuddleActivities.Description: Set the success criteria for technical work that customer investment would fund.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: For the proposed proof of concept or workshop, define what an investment-funded engagement would need to demonstrate, the observable success measures, the exit criteria and the evidence that would satisfy a reviewer. Do not assume the investment is approved.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Draft proof or workshop scope, customer decision criteria
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Success and exit criteria specific enough to justify and later evaluate an investment.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SE validates that the criteria are observable and that scope is bounded.
HuddleActivities.BestFitJob: Set the success criteria for technical work that customer investment would fund.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: This links PoC scope to investment readiness without implying the investment is approved.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build a reusable objection and language library from real calls
HuddleActivities.Description: Mine your own customer conversations for the objections and language that keep recurring, and turn them into something the team can reuse.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Work across my customer meeting transcripts and mail from the last quarter for [solution area]. Identify the objections that keep recurring, the language customers actually use to describe the problem we solve, the competitor claims that come up, and the points where conversations stall. Group them by how often they appear. For each recurring objection, show me the customer's own words rather than a paraphrase, and note which conversations it came from so I can go back to the source.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Confirm you can reach your own meeting transcripts and mail for this solution area.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Check the recurring objections against your own memory of those calls before treating them as a pattern.
4. Keep the customer language the customer actually used rather than rewriting it into product language.
5. Share the library with your solution area only after removing customer-identifying detail.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved access to your own meeting transcripts and mail; the solution area in scope; a quarter or more of conversations.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: An objection and customer-language library grouped by frequency, quoted in the customer's own words, traceable back to source conversations.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP verifies the quotes against the source conversation, removes anything customer-identifying before sharing, and decides what is safe to circulate beyond the account team.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The most useful competitive content is already sitting in conversations you have had. Reading a quarter of transcripts by hand is not realistic, which is why this pattern only became available recently.

HuddleActivities.Name: Assess investment fit and request readiness
HuddleActivities.Description: Assemble an investment readiness assessment without determining eligibility or approval.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using approved customer, opportunity, workload, partner, and engagement context, assemble an investment readiness assessment. Identify confirmed inputs, gaps, dependencies, and questions requiring a process owner. Do not determine final eligibility or approval.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Customer outcome; opportunity context; engagement intent; partner context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Readiness assessment with confirmed inputs, gaps, owners, and next decision.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP confirms source accuracy, current policy/process boundaries, role ownership, decision authority, and customer context.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Working through readiness forces a position without overstating authority.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build the request preparation package
HuddleActivities.Description: Organize approved investment inputs into a preparation package.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Organize approved investment inputs into a preparation package. Separate facts from assumptions, identify role contributions, and show unresolved dependencies. Do not submit, approve, or invent missing information.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved account, technical, delivery, partner, and outcome inputs.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Request preparation package with confirmed facts, open questions, contributions, and human decisions.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP confirms source accuracy, current policy/process boundaries, role ownership, decision authority, and customer context.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Most request delay is missing inputs and unclear ownership.

HuddleActivities.Name: Coordinate contributors, suppliers, and handoffs
HuddleActivities.Description: Map contributors, partner/supplier inputs, dependencies, and handoff points.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Map the contributors, partner or supplier inputs, dependencies, and handoff points for the proposed investment. Identify stalled items and owners. Do not imply funding or approval status.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Current request context and contributor information.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Contributor and handoff map with inputs, owners, dependencies, and escalation questions.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP confirms source accuracy, ownership, decision authority, and status before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Contributor handoffs are invisible when they work and obvious when they fail.

HuddleActivities.Name: Connect investment to the opportunity decision path
HuddleActivities.Description: Explain how investment supports the customer decision, milestones, readiness, and outcomes.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Explain how the proposed investment supports the customer decision, engagement milestones, implementation readiness, and intended outcomes. Separate evidence from assumptions and do not represent funding as approved.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Opportunity strategy; proposed investment; supported outcomes.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Investment-to-opportunity rationale with evidence, milestones, dependencies, and next decision.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP confirms the barrier is real, investment is an appropriate lever, and no approval or funding status is overstated.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Investment should connect to a customer decision, not sit beside the pursuit.

HuddleActivities.Name: Track request status and identify the next supported action
HuddleActivities.Description: Summarize current request stage, owner, blockers, and next supported action.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Summarize the current investment request stage, known owner, blockers, pending information, and next supported action using approved status sources. Do not claim unsupported editing, automation, eligibility, funding, or approval status.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved request status and notifications.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Status and next-action brief with owner, blockers, and questions.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP verifies current status against authoritative records before acting or reporting.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: With request status, the change finds you instead of you remembering to look.

HuddleActivities.Name: Submit the request and know where it went
HuddleActivities.Description: Move the prepared request into MSX Deal Assistance, confirm what is required before submission, and know how to check its status afterwards.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: I have a prepared investment request for [opportunity]. Before I submit it in MSX Deal Assistance, check my package against what a complete submission needs: opportunity linkage, business justification, ROI rationale, workscope reference, supplier detail if applicable, and the consumption plan if this is a Global ECIF or ACO request. Tell me what is missing or thin, and what an approver is most likely to send back. Do not tell me it is eligible or approvable; that is not your call.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Run the prompt against your prepared package.
2. Close whatever it flags as missing.
3. Open the opportunity in MSX, go to the Deal Assistance tab, select New Request, and choose the request type.
4. Attach the workscope from ECIF Central if the request needs one.
5. Submit, then note where the tracker view shows it sitting and who holds it.
6. If you are blocked on access or process rather than a decision, go to MCAPS Help rather than waiting.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The prepared request package. The MSX opportunity. The workscope from ECIF Central if applicable. Access to MSX Deal Assistance.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A submitted request with a known status, a named current owner, and a completeness check done before submission rather than after a rejection.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP confirms the business justification is genuine rather than assembled to pass a check, and accepts that eligibility, policy, and funding decisions belong to the accountable owners rather than to the seller or the tool.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A request that comes back for missing information costs a cycle. Most of what gets sent back is knowable before submission.

HuddleActivities.Name: Bring funding into the pursuit orchestration plan
HuddleActivities.Description: Add investment and funding path to the specialist and partner plan.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the current pursuit plan, identify where funding or customer investment is a dependency, who owns the request, what inputs are still missing, and the next governed action. Do not represent funding as approved.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Current pursuit plan; contributor list; known funding dependencies.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Pursuit plan with funding dependency, owner, and next action made explicit.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP confirms ownership of the request and that no funding status is overstated.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Funding is part of orchestration when it changes the pursuit path.

HuddleActivities.Name: Close the loop on outreach that never got an answer
HuddleActivities.Description: Track the outreach you have sent so the follow-ups that matter are surfaced and drafted rather than remembered.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review the outreach I have sent over the last 30 days and identify every message where I asked for something - a meeting, an introduction, a decision, or information - and did not receive a substantive reply. For each one, tell me how long it has been waiting, how important it looks based on the opportunity involved, and draft a short follow-up in my own voice that adds a new reason to respond rather than simply repeating the ask. Do not send anything.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Confirm the check can see your sent messages for the last 30 days.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Review the ranked list and remove any thread where the silence is itself the answer.
4. Edit every drafted follow-up so it adds a new reason to reply rather than repeating the ask.
5. Send them yourself; do not let the check send on your behalf.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Access to your sent messages; your current lead and opportunity list; your team's follow-up cadence norms.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A ranked list of unanswered asks with elapsed time and a drafted follow-up for each that adds new value rather than repeating.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP reviews and edits every draft before sending, and removes any follow-up where the silence is itself the answer.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Most lost specialist opportunities are not rejected - they are dropped. The follow-up that would have converted was never sent because it was never surfaced.

HuddleActivities.Name: Compare production architecture options
HuddleActivities.Description: Investigate current architecture patterns and evidence.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Research architecture options for [workload/customer scenario] using approved Microsoft and authoritative public sources. Compare security, resilience, governance, scale, operational complexity, cost considerations, dependencies and maturity. Cite claims, identify conflicting guidance or missing evidence, and do not recommend until decision criteria are explicit.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Outcome; workload; constraints; decision criteria; allowed sources.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Sourced option comparison.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSA validates source authority, applicability, security, compliance and recommendation boundaries.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Comparing production architecture options surfaces the difference that actually changes the decision.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the production-ready architecture package
HuddleActivities.Description: Produce a bounded architecture decision package.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Create a production-ready architecture decision package for [Customer/workload] using approved context and option analysis. Include desired outcome, current state, recommended architecture, alternative, tradeoffs, controls, governance, dependencies, sequence, readiness criteria, open decisions, and a human-review checklist. Stop and ask when evidence conflicts or a material decision lacks an owner.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved architecture context and reviewers.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Architecture decision package.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSA owns the recommendation and obtains required reviews.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: You spend your time editing the production-ready architecture package rather than staring at a blank version of it.

HuddleActivities.Name: Map approvals and fastest governed path
HuddleActivities.Description: Identify approval, policy and escalation dependencies.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review opportunity [ID] and map all known approvals, policy checks, reviewers, dependencies and escalation paths. Highlight blockers, missing evidence and the next action for each. Draft a Deal Desk justification, but do not submit it.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Opportunity ID and approved materials.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Approval map and draft justification.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CE validates approval requirements, evidence, routing, precedent and final submission.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Naming approvals and fastest governed path is most of the work. Unnamed problems never get an owner.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the commercial execution tracker
HuddleActivities.Description: Coordinate approvals, amendments and close actions.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using approved deal materials, create an execution tracker with action, owner, evidence, dependency, due checkpoint, status, blocker, escalation and decision required. Separate customer actions from internal actions.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved deal materials.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Commercial execution tracker.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CE confirms owners, dates, approvals, customer commitments and system-of-record updates.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: You spend your time editing the commercial execution tracker rather than staring at a blank version of it.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build the negotiation strategy and concession plan
HuddleActivities.Description: Prepare positions and value trades before negotiation.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Build a negotiation plan for [deal]. Include customer objectives, Microsoft objectives, opening position, must-have terms, tradable items, concession ladder, give/get logic, likely objections, walk-away or escalation triggers and next decision.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved deal and authority context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Negotiation and concession plan.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CE validates authority, customer context, policy, value trades and escalation triggers.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Most of the effort in the negotiation strategy and concession plan is assembly, and assembly is exactly what AI removes.

HuddleActivities.Name: Rehearse the commercial negotiation
HuddleActivities.Description: Practice objections, value trades and decision control.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Role-play the upcoming commercial negotiation using the approved plan. Simulate realistic customer objections and requests. Pause for my response, then coach clarity, value trading, concession discipline, policy boundaries and the next decision. Do not invent terms or authority.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved negotiation plan.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Negotiation rehearsal and coaching actions.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CE validates all positions, concessions, authority and customer commitments before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Ten minutes rehearsing the commercial negotiation is cheaper than improvising it in the room.

HuddleActivities.Name: Map eligibility, policy, and execution requirements
HuddleActivities.Description: Apply current authoritative guidance to a proposed structure and route open questions.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using current approved guidance and the proposed segment, products, SKUs, terms, agreement context, and exception questions, identify eligibility considerations, required amendments, execution steps, approval needs, side-agreement risk, and authoritative owners. Cite the exact guidance used and flag uncertainty. Do not approve exceptions.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Current approved guidance and proposed offer.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Policy, eligibility, and execution map with cited guidance, open questions, and owners.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CE validates source version, interpretation, required legal, finance, policy, or Deal Desk review, and any customer-facing use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The useful AI output is not a guessed policy answer. It is the right question, evidence, and owner.

HuddleActivities.Name: Inspect licensing, discount, and compliance risk
HuddleActivities.Description: Review the proposed structure for commercial risk.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review the proposed licensing, discount, and compliance structure for [account/opportunity]. Identify unused or mismatched licensing, discount exceptions, compliance concerns, policy questions, approval requirements, renewal risk, and evidence gaps. Cite sources where available.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Proposed licensing and discount structure.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Licensing, discount, and compliance risk review with evidence gaps and approval questions.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CE validates licensing, eligibility, discount authority, policy and recommended action.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Reviewing licensing and discount risk is judgment work. The agent proposes; the CE remains accountable.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build the CE-led renewal strategy view
HuddleActivities.Description: Surface renewal economics, risk and expansion early.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: For [account name or TPID], show the upcoming renewals with expiry dates and current agreement details, then for the agreement I name provide the license estate grouped by SKU, the SKUs whose discount is between 40 and 60 percent, and ACR trends month over month. Build a CE-led renewal strategy view covering structure, MACC trajectory, consumption signals, current discounts and concessions, risk, expansion potential, and amendments in play. Separate what the source systems returned from what you inferred, and do not represent any concession or discount as approved.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Account and approved renewal context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Renewal strategy brief with commercial structure, risk, expansion potential, approval path, and evidence gaps.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CE validates contract, revenue, usage, structure, risk, authority and ownership.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Most of the effort in the renewal strategy view is assembly. The strategy decision stays human-led.

HuddleActivities.Name: Inspect upcoming renewal portfolio for CE intervention
HuddleActivities.Description: Prioritize renewals requiring CE intervention.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Show upcoming renewals in the selected period for my scope. Prioritize by revenue, discount exposure, consumption or MACC risk, execution complexity, expansion potential, approval requirements, and evidence quality. Explain the certified signal behind each priority.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved renewal report and scope.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Prioritized renewal radar with intervention rationale, evidence quality, and missing data.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CE validates report scope, signals, ownership and recommended intervention.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Reviewing the renewal portfolio is judgment work. The agent proposes; the CE stays accountable.

HuddleActivities.Name: Identify commercial risk and escalation priorities
HuddleActivities.Description: Use approved signals to prioritize commercial risk, source evidence, and escalation needs.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review the approved commercial, renewal, agreement, and deal signals for [scope]. Identify the top commercial risks, the supporting source signal, likely impact, recommended intervention, owner, escalation need, and any unavailable or stale data. Separate evidence from interpretation.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved scope, current commercial signals, renewal or agreement context, and known ownership.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Prioritized commercial risk view with evidence, intervention, owner, escalation need, and source gaps.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CE validates data scope, source freshness, business context, risk interpretation, mitigation, owner, and escalation route.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Commercial risk found early is a conversation. The same risk found at approval becomes delay.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build the commercial decision brief
HuddleActivities.Description: Prepare commercial talking points, decision needs, and authority boundaries for a live customer or deal review.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Prepare the CE commercial decision brief for [account/opportunity]. Include contract context, proposed structure, concessions or terms requiring review, current approvals, renewal or consumption risk, likely customer questions, authority boundaries, and the next commercial decision. Flag any customer-facing claim requiring review.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Account or opportunity context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Commercial decision brief with authority boundaries, risks, questions, and next decision.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CE validates terms, authority, source freshness, customer-facing positions, and required reviewers.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Most of the effort in the commercial decision brief is assembly. The judgment stays with the CE.

HuddleActivities.Name: Compare viable commercial structures
HuddleActivities.Description: Develop decision-ready commercial options.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: For [opportunity], compare three viable commercial structures using available approved context. For each show products or SKUs, term, pricing logic, customer value, Microsoft trade-offs, risks, approvals and assumptions. Do not create or submit an offer.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved opportunity context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Commercial options matrix.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CE validates pricing, products, licensing, authority, policy and feasibility.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Comparing viable commercial structures surfaces the difference that actually changes the decision.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the commercial decision narrative
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn approved context into a concise internal recommendation.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the approved deal context and options, draft a commercial decision narrative with customer outcome, options considered, recommended structure, value trades, assumptions, risks, required reviewers and next decision.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved deal context and options.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Internal commercial recommendation.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CE approves the recommendation and routes required review.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: You spend your time editing the commercial decision narrative rather than staring at a blank version of it.

HuddleActivities.Name: Research agreement and commerce changes
HuddleActivities.Description: Ground migration advice in current authoritative sources.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Research current differences between [legacy agreement] and [new commerce model] using authoritative Microsoft sources. Summarize commercial, administrative and customer-impact differences, risks, unresolved questions and citations.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Agreement models and authoritative sources.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Sourced transition evidence brief.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CE and policy, licensing or legal SMEs validate applicability and current guidance.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Being able to cite agreement and commerce changes beats being able to remember it.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build the customer migration brief
HuddleActivities.Description: Translate approved guidance into customer-specific decision support.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using approved customer contract context and validated transition guidance, create a migration brief with current state, contractual differences, administrative shift, amendment needs, red-line risks, choices, timeline, responsibilities and customer talk track.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved contract context and validated guidance.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Customer-specific migration brief.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CE validates contract interpretation, policy, dates, commitments and required reviewers.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Most of the effort in the customer migration brief is assembly, and assembly is exactly what AI removes.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build the competitive differentiation brief
HuddleActivities.Description: Use approved win/loss and market context for a proof-backed competitive position.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Produce a competitive differentiation brief for [solution area] and [customer context]. Include relevant win/loss drivers, three strongest differentiators with proof, common objections with handlers, risks, and a concise talk track. Flag where data or proof is weak.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Solution area; customer context; approved competitive and win/loss sources.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Competitive brief with differentiators, proof, objections, and talk track.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP validates freshness, source grounding, customer applicability, and claims before external use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Competitive conversations are lost by improvisation.

HuddleActivities.Name: Research competitive and industry context
HuddleActivities.Description: Investigate current evidence before positioning.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Research [competitor], [solution area], and [customer industry]. Compare publicly supportable positions, proof, recent developments, common objections, and uncertainty. Do not infer confidential competitor information.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Competitor; solution area; industry; approved source boundaries.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Sourced competitive context brief.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP validates source quality, timeliness, relevance, and customer-facing claims.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Being able to cite competitive context beats remembering it.

HuddleActivities.Name: Test the differentiator against the customer's real decision criteria
HuddleActivities.Description: Pressure-test each claimed differentiator against what this customer actually said they will decide on, and drop the ones that do not connect.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: You are helping a specialist seller sharpen a competitive position. Here is the customer's stated decision criteria and evaluation process: [paste criteria, evaluation team, timeline]. Here are the differentiators we plan to lead with: [paste differentiators and proof]. For each differentiator, state which specific decision criterion it addresses, how directly it addresses it, and what proof the customer would need to accept it. Identify any differentiator that does not map to a stated criterion and recommend dropping or reframing it. Flag any criterion we currently have no answer for. Do not add differentiators that are not in my list.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Gather the customer's stated decision criteria from meeting notes or MSX.
2. List current differentiators and their proof.
3. Run the prompt.
4. Cut differentiators that do not map to a criterion.
5. Name the gaps you cannot yet answer.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Customer decision criteria and evaluation process; current differentiators and supporting proof; who is on the evaluation team.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A shortened differentiator list mapped to decision criteria, plus a named list of criteria with no current answer.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP confirms the decision criteria are what the customer actually said rather than what the team assumes, and owns the decision to drop a differentiator.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A differentiator the customer is not deciding on is noise, however true it is.

HuddleActivities.Name: Rehearse the competitive conversation and build the objection handler
HuddleActivities.Description: Practice the response out loud, then convert what broke into a written objection handler tied to approved proof.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Play the role of a technical evaluator at [customer] who currently favors [competitor]. I will present our competitive position. Challenge me the way that evaluator would, including on price, migration effort, and lock-in. After three exchanges, stop the role-play and produce an objection handler table: each objection you raised, my response, the approved proof that supports it, and a note where no approved proof exists. Do not soften the objections and do not supply proof I have not given you.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Bring the differentiator list from the previous activity and the approved competitive proof.
2. Run a short rehearsal with the agent as the skeptical evaluator.
3. Have it produce the objection handler table.
4. Fill or remove any row where proof is missing.
5. Bring the table to the huddle.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Competitive position and differentiators; the competitor in play; approved competitive proof sources; known evaluator concerns; customer role you will be speaking to.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: An objection handler table mapping each objection to a response and the approved proof behind it, with proof gaps named.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP judges whether the rehearsed language is accurate, appropriate for this customer, and consistent with approved competitive guidance before using it externally.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Competitive conversations are lost in the moment, not in the brief.

HuddleActivities.Name: Convert the competitive position into the next customer step
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn the position into a concrete next action in the opportunity rather than a document that stops at the brief.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using this competitive position and the customer's decision criteria [paste], propose the single next step that would most reduce competitive risk in this opportunity. Give me three options ranked by impact, each with: what it is, who from our side needs to be involved, what the customer gets out of it, and what evidence it would generate for the decision. Then draft the short note I would send to the customer to set it up. Keep the note under 120 words and do not overstate what we have proven.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Bring the tested differentiator list and the open gaps.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Pick one next step.
4. Adjust the draft note in your own voice.
5. Record the next step in the opportunity.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Tested differentiators and open gaps; opportunity stage and close plan; who owns the customer relationship.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: One chosen next step with owner and purpose, and a short customer-ready note to set it up.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP owns the choice of next step and the customer-facing wording, and confirms it fits the account team's plan before sending.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A competitive brief that does not change the next customer interaction has not changed the deal.

HuddleActivities.Name: Analyze consumption trajectory and shortfall drivers
HuddleActivities.Description: Ask what certified consumption data says.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: For [Customer] and [period], analyze enabled consumption trajectory and compare it with the relevant plan or milestone view. Break down largest changes by available dimension, identify data-supported contributors to potential shortfall, show supporting metrics and state what the report cannot answer.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Enabled certified report; customer; period.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Consumption trajectory analysis.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSA confirms scope, KPI definitions, technical significance and credibility.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Working through consumption trajectory and shortfall drivers forces a position, and a position is what the decision needs.

HuddleActivities.Name: Design a technical shortfall intervention
HuddleActivities.Description: Connect customer context to intervention planning.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using approved consumption analysis and available context for [Customer], identify technical blockers, workload milestones, stakeholders, commitments and dependencies relevant to the potential shortfall. Propose intervention options, owner candidates, customer touchpoints and evidence needed. Do not assume cause or make commitments.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved analysis and authorized context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Intervention options with evidence, owners and gaps.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSA selects intervention and validates cause, context, ownership and commitments.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Settling a technical shortfall intervention before the work starts is the only version of that decision that holds.

HuddleActivities.Name: Rehearse the executive customer conversation
HuddleActivities.Description: Rehearse the executive customer conversation
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Use Agent J.ai to role-play the upcoming [meeting type] with [customer or stakeholder]. Use the approved conversation plan and focus on the AE contribution: executive narrative, customer outcome, primary ask, fallback ask, likely questions, and relationship-sensitive responses. Simulate realistic questions or objections, pause for the team member response, then provide coaching on clarity, evidence, listening, and the proposed next step. Identify claims, commitments, technical guidance, or commercial positions that require human or SME review. Do not invent customer facts or make commitments.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved conversation plan; meeting type; customer or stakeholder context; role contribution; desired decision or outcome; known boundaries.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Role-play output with likely questions, coaching observations, improvement actions, and claims requiring review.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: AE validates customer facts, commitments, technical or commercial guidance, and final wording before customer use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Rehearsal lets weak claims fail safely before the customer hears them.

HuddleActivities.Name: Prepare the solution-specific customer conversation
HuddleActivities.Description: Build grounded discovery, proof, objection, role contribution, and ask structure.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Prepare me for the upcoming [meeting] with [account]. Summarize priorities, stakeholders, open risks, competitive mentions, and solution context. Draft five discovery questions, proof points, likely objections with responses, role contributions, primary ask, and fallback ask. Flag uncertainty.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Account; meeting; solution play; current stage; approved sales context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Conversation plan with discovery questions, proof, objections, role contributions, and ask.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP validates customer facts, evidence, competitive claims, commitments, and the final ask.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Preparation is where the solution conversation is decided.

HuddleActivities.Name: Find the discovery gap before the meeting, not after
HuddleActivities.Description: Check what you still do not know that would change your recommendation, and build the question that closes it.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Here is what we currently know about [account] for [solution play]: [paste priorities, environment, stakeholders, constraints, prior conversations]. Identify what we do not know that would materially change our recommendation, ranked by how much it would change it. For the top three unknowns, write one open question each that could be asked naturally in the upcoming conversation without sounding like a survey. Distinguish what we actually know from what we have assumed.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Assemble what is known about the account.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Separate known from assumed.
4. Choose one question to definitely ask.
5. Add it to the conversation plan.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Everything currently known about the account and solution context; prior conversation notes; the recommendation you intend to make.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A ranked list of decision-changing unknowns and three natural questions to close the top ones.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP verifies which items are genuinely known versus assumed by the account team, and chooses which question is worth the meeting time.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The most expensive assumptions are the ones nobody noticed they were making.

HuddleActivities.Name: Turn the conversation into decisions and commitments
HuddleActivities.Description: Convert meeting notes into what changed, what was agreed, and what the customer actually committed to.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Here are my notes from the customer conversation: [paste notes or transcript summary]. Produce three separate lists: what we learned that changes our understanding, what was explicitly agreed and by whom, and what remains open. Then draft a short follow-up note to the customer confirming only what was actually agreed. Do not record something as agreed if the notes only show it was discussed. Flag anything ambiguous rather than resolving it.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Capture notes immediately after the meeting.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Check the agreed list against your memory.
4. Send the follow-up note.
5. Update the opportunity with what changed.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Meeting notes or transcript summary; who attended; what was asked for; the conversation plan you went in with.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Separated lists of learnings, agreements, and open items, plus a short confirming follow-up note.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP confirms that anything recorded as agreed was actually agreed, and owns the follow-up wording before sending.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Deals slip on the gap between what was discussed and what was agreed.

HuddleActivities.Name: Rehearse solution discovery and objection handling
HuddleActivities.Description: Rehearse the solution conversation and receive coaching before customer use.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Use Agent J.ai to role-play the upcoming [meeting type] with [customer or stakeholder]. Use the approved conversation plan and focus on solution discovery, differentiation, proof points, likely objections, next solution decision, and primary ask. Pause for the team member response, then coach clarity, evidence, listening, and next step. Do not invent customer facts or commitments.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved conversation plan; meeting type; customer context; desired outcome.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Interactive role-play, targeted coaching, objections, and improvement list.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP validates facts, claims, commitments, guidance, and decides what to change before customer use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Ten minutes rehearsing is cheaper than improvising in the room.

HuddleActivities.Name: Inspect solution opportunity readiness
HuddleActivities.Description: Identify the decision or blocker preventing progression.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review opportunity [ID] for [solution play]. Summarize current stage, customer outcome, stakeholder coverage, proof or demo status, technical and commercial dependencies, partner or funding needs, blockers, and the single next decision required. Recommend actions with owners.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Opportunity ID; solution play; current sales context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Readiness view with blockers, next decision, actions, and owners.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP validates stage, blockers, owners, dependencies, and commitments.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Readiness inspection is judgment work. The agent proposes; the SSP stays accountable.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the solution acceleration action plan
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn enabled opportunity data into prioritized actions.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: For my active [solution area] opportunities, identify stalled milestones, missing customer evidence, stakeholder gaps, and next actions. Prioritize the opportunities requiring SSP intervention this week.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Enabled MSXI report or opportunity context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Prioritized solution-opportunity action plan.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP validates report scope, stage, risk, intervention, and ownership.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The path advances when blockers, owners, and next decisions are explicit.

HuddleActivities.Name: Prepare the conversation that clears the next decision
HuddleActivities.Description: Design the single conversation that would unblock the opportunity, and decide who needs to be in it.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: For opportunity [ID], the next decision required is [paste decision] and the current blocker is [paste blocker]. Design the one conversation that would most likely clear it: who needs to be in the room from both sides, what each person needs to hear, what we must bring as evidence, what we are asking them to decide by the end, and what we do if they say not yet. Keep it to one conversation; do not propose a sequence of three meetings.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Bring the readiness view and the named blocker.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Confirm the attendee list is realistic.
4. Prepare the evidence.
5. Schedule it.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The readiness view; the next decision required; the current blocker; stakeholder coverage; available evidence and proof.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A single conversation design with attendees, evidence needed, the decision being asked for, and a fallback.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP validates that the named blocker is the real one, confirms attendees with the account team, and owns what is asked of the customer.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Most stalled opportunities need one specific conversation, not more activity.

HuddleActivities.Name: State the close plan in the customer's terms
HuddleActivities.Description: Rewrite the close plan as the customer's path to their outcome, so it can be shared with them rather than kept internal.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Rewrite this internal close plan [paste] as a shared plan from the customer's point of view. Replace our sales stages with their decision milestones, name what they need from us at each step and what we need from them, and end with the outcome they said they wanted. Remove internal language, forecast terms, and anything we would not want a customer to read. Flag any step that depends on something we have not confirmed with them.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Bring the internal close plan.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Remove anything still internal.
4. Check every date is one the customer has agreed to.
5. Share it and ask them to correct it.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The internal close plan; the customer's stated outcome and decision process; confirmed dates versus assumed dates.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A customer-facing shared plan organized around their decision milestones, with unconfirmed dependencies flagged.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP verifies no internal forecast language survives, confirms which dates the customer actually agreed to, and approves before sharing externally.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A close plan the customer has never seen is a forecast, not a plan.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build a prioritized lead follow-up plan
HuddleActivities.Description: Combine scattered lead, event, account, and interaction signals into a structured SSP follow-up plan.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using approved lead, attendee, account, email, meeting, and public context, create a prioritized follow-up plan for [solution area]. For each lead include source, account, likely interest, solution relevance, suggested message, owner, and next action. Flag missing evidence and do not send outreach.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved lead or attendee lists; account context; solution area; recent interactions.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Prioritized lead follow-up plan with source, fit, message, owner, and next action.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP validates consent, customer context, solution relevance, ownership, and outreach language before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Most of the effort in lead follow-up is assembly. AI can assemble; the SSP decides where to focus.

HuddleActivities.Name: Identify missed solution-area opportunities
HuddleActivities.Description: Use sales signals to identify solution-area opportunities the SSP may be missing.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: For [solution area] across my active accounts, identify opportunity signals I may be missing. Show the source signal, likely customer need, relevant solution play, uncertainty, and the next discovery action. Separate facts from recommendations.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: SSP scope; solution area; available MSX and approved customer signals.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Ranked opportunity hypotheses with next discovery actions.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP validates signal quality, customer need, ownership, and whether an opportunity should be created or advanced.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Unnamed solution opportunities never get an owner.

HuddleActivities.Name: Draft the first contact for the top-priority lead
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn the top-ranked lead into a specific, short first message that connects the signal to a reason for the customer to respond.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Here is the top lead from my follow-up plan: [paste source signal, account, role, likely interest, and any prior interaction].
