Draft a first contact message under 100 words that references the specific signal, states one reason this is relevant to their business now, and asks for one small next step. Give me two versions: one for a business decision maker and one for a technical decision maker. Do not claim knowledge of their environment we do not have, and do not assert a product feature I have not given you.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Take the top lead from the prioritized plan.
2. Confirm consent and context are appropriate for outreach.
3. Run the prompt.
4. Edit into your own voice.
5. Send one, and note the date.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The prioritized lead plan; the source signal; the contact's role; prior interaction history; consent and outreach appropriateness.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Two short first-contact drafts, one business and one technical, tied to the originating signal.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP confirms consent and outreach appropriateness, verifies every factual statement about the customer, and owns the wording before sending.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A prioritized list that never becomes a message is just a better-sorted backlog.

HuddleActivities.Name: Close the loop on what the follow-up produced
HuddleActivities.Description: Review the leads worked this week, record what happened, and decide which signals are worth trusting next time.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Here are the leads I followed up this week and what happened with each: [paste lead, source signal, action taken, response or silence]. Tell me which signal sources produced a response and which did not, what the responses have in common, and which two signal types I should prioritize next week. Be direct about small sample size; do not overstate a pattern from a handful of leads.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. List the leads worked and the outcome of each.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Record the outcome in the opportunity or lead record.
4. Name the one signal source you will deprioritize.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The leads worked this week; the originating signal for each; the action taken; the response or lack of one.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A short read on which signal sources are working, and one prioritization change for next week.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP judges whether the pattern is real or coincidence given the sample size, and owns the decision to change prioritization.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Lead follow-up improves only if you find out which signals were worth following.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build the optimization evidence base
HuddleActivities.Description: Analyze enabled usage, cost and consumption evidence.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: For [Customer] and [period], summarize enabled usage, consumption and cost signals relevant to optimization. Identify material changes and patterns visible in the report and supporting metrics. Separate observations from recommendations and state missing architecture or business context.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Enabled certified report and scope.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Optimization evidence summary.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSA confirms KPI meaning, architecture context, priorities and actionability.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Most of the effort in the optimization evidence base is assembly, and assembly is exactly what AI removes.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the FinOps and optimization recommendation
HuddleActivities.Description: Produce a bounded optimization recommendation.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using approved evidence, create an optimization recommendation for [Customer/workload]. Include current state, outcome, options, supported technical and financial effect, architecture tradeoffs, dependencies, risks, milestones and human-review requirements. Do not invent savings or intent.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved evidence; architecture context; outcome; constraints.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Optimization recommendation.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSA validates architecture, feasibility, claims, relevance and ownership.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: You spend your time editing the FinOps and optimization recommendation rather than staring at a blank version of it.

HuddleActivities.Name: Compare architecture options against decision criteria
HuddleActivities.Description: Investigate external technical patterns and authoritative evidence.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Research [architecture decision] using current authoritative Microsoft and approved customer sources. Compare viable options against [decision criteria], identify assumptions, risks, dependencies and evidence gaps, and cite each material claim.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Architecture decision; decision criteria; approved sources.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Sourced architecture options assessment.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SE and architecture SMEs validate current guidance, applicability and unsupported assumptions.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Comparing architecture options and evidence surfaces the difference that actually changes the decision.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the architecture decision record
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn approved evidence into a concise decision artifact.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the approved discovery brief and architecture evidence, create a decision record with customer outcome, options considered, criteria, selected direction, risks, dependencies, validation steps, unresolved questions and next technical action.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved discovery brief and architecture evidence.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Architecture decision record.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SE validates architecture, security, operations, feasibility and customer commitments.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: You spend your time editing the architecture decision record rather than staring at a blank version of it.

HuddleActivities.Name: Package a reusable technical asset with context
HuddleActivities.Description: Convert successful work into a repeatable, governed asset.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the approved [demo, script, architecture, response or checklist], create a reusable asset package with purpose, prerequisites, steps, editable parameters, validation checks, known limitations, owner and example use.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved technical asset.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Reusable asset package.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SE removes sensitive content, validates technical accuracy and confirms reuse permissions.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Reuse happens when the asset includes enough context for another SE to trust and adapt it.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create a technical Skill Blueprint for a repeatable SE workflow
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn a repeatable workflow into a structured personalized skill.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Create a reusable Skill Blueprint for [SE workflow]. Define trigger, inputs, trusted sources, ordered steps, expected output, rules, exclusions, exception behavior, human review, validation checks, and one representative test case. Do not publish until tested.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Choose the asset worth reusing.
2. Invoke the skill in Scout or Cowork.
3. Review the generated structure at the checkpoint.
4. Add the context a colleague would need.
5. Publish where the team will actually look.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: SE workflow; trusted sources; test case.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Technical Skill Blueprint with validation checks and test case.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SE or skill owner tests representative work and validates access, outputs, safeguards, and repository placement before promotion.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A blueprint lets the team test repeatability before pretending the skill is production-ready.

HuddleActivities.Name: Inspect technical deal health and proof gaps
HuddleActivities.Description: Use available MSX and customer context to identify technical progression gaps.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review [opportunity] and summarize the intended customer decision, current technical stage, exit criteria, proof completed, open blockers, recent technical engagement, missing roles and next recommended technical action. Show the source signal and flag unavailable context.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Opportunity and available customer context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Technical deal-health brief.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SE validates MSX accuracy, customer context, technical risk and the next action.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Technical deal health improves when blockers, proof gaps, and next decisions are visible in one place.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the technical risk and handoff plan
HuddleActivities.Description: Synthesize approved deal, proof and delivery context into an action plan.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using approved sources, create a technical risk and handoff plan with blocker, impact, evidence, owner, mitigation, checkpoint, decision needed and delivery handoff requirements.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved deal, proof and delivery sources.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Technical risk register and handoff plan.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SE confirms ownership, feasibility, customer commitments and delivery readiness.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Risk plans help only when they assign the owner, evidence, mitigation, checkpoint, and next decision.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build the decision-centered demo or workshop plan
HuddleActivities.Description: Create a bounded multi-part experience package.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Create a demo or workshop package for [customer decision]. Include audience, scenario, decision criteria, agenda, demo flow, sample data needs, roles, likely objections, tenant or permission dependencies, fallback plan and explicit next decision.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Customer decision; audience; approved scenario.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Demo or workshop package.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SE validates the environment, permissions, technical behavior, evidence and customer appropriateness.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A decision-centered plan keeps the demo or workshop from becoming a feature tour.

HuddleActivities.Name: Research supporting proof, limitations, and objections
HuddleActivities.Description: Find authoritative evidence supporting the selected scenario.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Find current authoritative evidence for [scenario or capability]. Return only claims relevant to the customer decision, likely objections, known limitations and SME-needed flags. Cite sources.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Scenario or capability; approved sources.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Evidence and objection brief.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SE validates freshness and applicability before customer use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Authoritative proof and known limitations are what make the demo safe to use in a customer decision.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build the technical discovery and decision-criteria brief
HuddleActivities.Description: Synthesize approved customer and technical context into a brief that names the customer decision, constraints, evidence gaps, and criteria.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the selected approved customer and technical sources, prepare for [meeting]. Summarize known outcomes, decisions, constraints, architecture context, open technical questions and missing evidence. Propose five discovery questions that advance the technical decision. Separate sourced facts from hypotheses.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Selected approved customer and technical sources.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Technical discovery brief with questions and evidence gaps.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SE validates the sources, technical context and whether each question is appropriate.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Discovery becomes useful when it produces decision criteria the customer and team can inspect.

HuddleActivities.Name: Rehearse the technical discovery conversation
HuddleActivities.Description: Practice questions, listening, objections and the intended next decision.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Role-play [customer or stakeholder] for the upcoming technical discovery conversation. Use the approved brief only. Simulate realistic questions and objections, coach clarity and listening, and identify statements requiring technical or customer validation. Do not invent customer facts.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved discovery brief.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Role-play, coaching observations and improvement actions.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SE verifies facts, claims and commitments and decides what to change.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Practicing discovery questions reduces the chance that the real meeting ends with ambiguity instead of criteria.

HuddleActivities.Name: Scope the smallest useful PoC
HuddleActivities.Description: Build the PoC work package.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Create a PoC plan for [technical decision]. Define hypothesis, in-scope scenario, success and exit criteria, milestones, data and environment needs, roles, risks, dependencies, review gates, final decision and handoff if successful.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Technical decision; constraints; resources.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: PoC plan and decision gates.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SE confirms scope, resources, security, feasibility and that the PoC is necessary.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A small, criteria-led PoC reduces waste and makes the exit decision clear before work starts.

HuddleActivities.Name: Pressure-test PoC readiness
HuddleActivities.Description: Review a proposed PoC plan for gaps and ambiguity.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review this PoC plan. Identify vague success criteria, unowned dependencies, unrealistic milestones, missing security or data assumptions, weak linkage to the customer decision and unclear exit paths. Return five review questions and the smallest revisions needed.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Proposed PoC plan.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Readiness review and revision list.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SE owns the go or no-go decision and confirms all required reviewers.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Readiness issues should be found in planning, not after the customer expects a proof.

HuddleActivities.Name: Draft the sourced technical answer matrix
HuddleActivities.Description: Answer technical questions with sources, confidence, assumptions, exceptions, and reviewer flags.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Answer the selected technical questions using approved and authoritative sources. For each item provide a grounded answer, source citation, confidence, assumptions and SME-needed flag. Preserve the question order and do not hide unsupported areas.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Selected technical questions; approved sources.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Grounded technical answer matrix.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SE and relevant SMEs approve technical, security, legal and product claims.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A technical answer is safer when confidence, assumptions, and reviewer needs are visible.

HuddleActivities.Name: Assemble the governed technical response package
HuddleActivities.Description: Produce reviewed answers in the required structure and coordinate gaps.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the approved answer matrix, assemble the response in the requested format. Create an exception list for unanswered items, assign suggested reviewers and provide a final quality checklist. Do not submit or send.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved answer matrix; required format.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Formatted response plus exception list.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SE validates completeness and obtains required approvals before distribution.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Governance is what keeps fast response work from becoming unsupported customer guidance.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build the solution-selling plan
HuddleActivities.Description: Shape a solution-specific plan to advance the next customer decision.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Build a solution-selling plan for [solution play] at [account]. Include customer outcomes, maturity, solution vision, stakeholder coverage, value conversation arc, demo or workshop sequence, proof needs, risks, and a 30-day plan to clear the next decision. Flag missing stakeholders and unsupported claims.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Account; solution play; current stage; known stakeholders; approved evidence.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Solution-selling plan with decisions, proof needs, owners, and progression actions.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP validates customer need, stage, solution fit, evidence, stakeholders, and commitments.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Most of the solution-selling plan is assembly; the SSP should spend judgment on the pursuit decision.

HuddleActivities.Name: Pressure-test the solution strategy
HuddleActivities.Description: Test the plan against customer priorities, competitive alternatives, stakeholders, and decision criteria.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review this solution-selling plan against customer priorities, competitive alternatives, stakeholder coverage, proof needs, technical and commercial dependencies, and decision criteria. Return risks, gaps, missing evidence, and the next decisions needed.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Draft solution-selling plan; customer context; stakeholder map; proof and constraints.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Pressure-tested strategy with risks, gaps, and next decisions.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP confirms source accuracy, customer context, role ownership, technical/commercial dependencies, and any system action before use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: If the solution strategy will fail, it should fail in review before it fails with the customer.

HuddleActivities.Name: Map who actually decides and who is missing
HuddleActivities.Description: Build the real decision map for this solution play, including the people who can stop it, not only the people who like it.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Here is my solution-selling plan and the stakeholders I have engaged: [paste plan and stakeholder list with roles and engagement level]. The solution play is [paste], the decision type is [paste, for example new workload, renewal, or migration], the customer's organizational model is [paste, for example centralized IT, business-unit autonomy, or shared services], and their known procurement and technical governance constraints are [paste]. Build a decision map showing who decides, who influences, who implements, and who can block. For each person, state what they need to believe for this to move forward and what evidence would convince them. Then identify missing roles ONLY where the solution play, decision type, organizational model, or governance constraints I gave you imply that role is required. Do not list generic enterprise buying-committee roles. Do not invent names; describe missing roles by function. If my context is too thin to identify missing roles, say so rather than guessing.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. List stakeholders engaged so far with role and engagement level.
2. Gather the solution play, decision type, customer organizational model, and governance constraints.
3. Run the prompt.
4. Identify the highest-risk absence.
5. Decide who introduces you to that person and by when.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Solution-selling plan; stakeholders engaged with roles; the solution play and decision type; the customer's organizational model; known procurement and technical governance constraints; who owns the customer relationship.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A decision map with what each stakeholder needs to believe, plus a named list of missing roles and the risk each creates.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP validates the stakeholder reality against what the account team actually knows, and owns the plan to reach anyone missing.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Solution plans usually fail on a person nobody engaged, not on a fact nobody knew.

HuddleActivities.Name: Convert the plan into dated commitments
HuddleActivities.Description: Reduce the plan to the few actions that will actually happen in the next 30 days, each with a named owner and a date.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: From this solution-selling plan [paste], extract only the actions that must happen in the next 30 days to clear the next customer decision. For each: what it is, who owns it by role, the date it must be done by, and what it unblocks. Limit to five actions. If the plan implies more than five critical actions in 30 days, tell me which ones are not realistic and what to cut. Do not assign an action to a person or team I have not named.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Bring the pressure-tested plan.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Cut to five or fewer.
4. Confirm each owner has agreed.
5. Record the dates where the account team will see them.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The pressure-tested solution-selling plan; the account team and their availability; the next customer decision and its timing.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Five or fewer dated actions with named owners and what each unblocks.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP confirms each owner has actually agreed to the action and the date, rather than being assigned it in a document.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A plan without dates and owners is a description of intentions.

HuddleActivities.Name: Prepare the technical advisory conversation
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn approved evidence into a customer-centered plan.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using approved customer context and technical decision package, prepare for [meeting]. Include outcome, technical state, recommendation and tradeoffs, questions, supporting evidence, likely objections, caveats, next action and ownership. Flag claims requiring review.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved context; technical package; desired decision.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Technical advisory conversation plan.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSA validates claims, tradeoffs, context, commitments and follow-through.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Preparation for the technical advisory conversation is the step most often skipped and most often decisive.

HuddleActivities.Name: Rehearse the architecture recommendation
HuddleActivities.Description: Role-play and coach a technical advisory conversation.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Use the approved conversation plan to role-play with [customer/stakeholder]. Simulate realistic architecture, readiness, security, operational, cost and implementation questions. Coach clarity, evidence, listening, tradeoffs and next step. Identify claims needing SME review. Do not invent customer facts or commitments.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved conversation plan and audience.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Role-play transcript and improvement actions.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSA validates facts, guidance, claims and commitments.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Ten minutes rehearsing the architecture recommendation is cheaper than improvising it in the room.

HuddleActivities.Name: Tailor the solution value narrative
HuddleActivities.Description: Translate the solution into customer-specific outcomes, evidence, caveats, and next ask.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using selected approved sources, build a customer-specific value narrative for [solution play] at [account]. Include top use cases, measurable or directional outcomes, proof points, differentiation, assumptions, caveats, executive talking points, and the next ask. Flag unsupported value claims.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved customer priorities, solution evidence, value frameworks, and target audience.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Customer-specific value narrative with evidence and review flags.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP validates value claims, proof, ROI or adoption assumptions, tone, and final ask before customer use.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Generic value decks lose to specific narratives grounded in customer priorities.

HuddleActivities.Name: Research evidence for the value story
HuddleActivities.Description: Investigate customer, industry, use-case, and market evidence that strengthens or challenges the value story.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Research [customer/industry/use case] to identify relevant market evidence, customer signals, comparable proof, risks, and counterevidence for [solution play]. Separate sourced facts from recommendations and flag unsupported value or competitor claims.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Customer; industry; use case; solution play; approved source boundaries.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Evidence brief for the value narrative.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP validates source quality, applicability to the customer, and all value or competitor claims.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Being able to cite value evidence beats remembering a generic claim.

HuddleActivities.Name: Stress-test the assumptions the value claims depend on
HuddleActivities.Description: Expose what each outcome number quietly assumes, and record which assumptions the customer would have to accept.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Here is our value narrative and the evidence brief behind it: [paste both]. For every outcome claim, produce a row containing: the claim, the assumption it depends on, who has to accept that assumption for the claim to hold, the evidence we currently have, and what happens to the claim if adoption is half as fast as projected. Rank the rows by how much the claim collapses when its assumption fails. Do not add claims that are not in my narrative, and do not supply evidence I have not given you.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Bring the value narrative and evidence brief.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Find the claim that collapses hardest.
4. Either find proof for its assumption or remove the claim.
5. Bring the assumption table to the huddle.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The value narrative; the evidence brief; the customer's financial context; adoption expectations already discussed with them.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: An assumption and risk table ranked by how much each claim depends on an unproven assumption.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP decides which assumptions are defensible with this customer, and owns every outcome figure before it reaches them.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The value claim you cannot defend is the one the customer will ask about.

HuddleActivities.Name: Reduce the narrative to something the customer can forward
HuddleActivities.Description: Produce the short version your champion can send to people you will never meet, without you in the room to explain it.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Reduce this value narrative [paste] to a single page that our champion could forward internally without us present. It must stand alone: state the business problem in the customer's own terms, the outcome, what it depends on, and what we are asking for next. Remove anything that only makes sense if a seller is explaining it. Remove any claim that is not supported by the evidence brief I gave you. Keep it under 350 words.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Bring the rehearsed narrative with weak claims removed.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Read it as if you were a stranger receiving it.
4. Cut anything that needs explaining.
5. Confirm the ask is specific.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The rehearsed value narrative; the evidence brief; who the champion is and who they would forward it to; the next ask.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A one-page, forwardable value summary with a specific next ask.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP verifies every claim survives without a seller present, and approves the wording before the champion receives it.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Most internal customer decisions happen in rooms the seller is not in.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the technical progress and value narrative
HuddleActivities.Description: Synthesize approved technical evidence.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using approved architecture, delivery, adoption, consumption, optimization and risk materials for [Customer], create the CSA contribution to the business review. Connect progress to supported outcomes, explain risks and decisions, identify commitments and owners, and propose next technical actions. Separate evidence from interpretation and flag unsupported value claims.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved review sources; audience; period.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Technical progress and value narrative.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSA validates technical and value claims, linkage, commitments and ownership.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: You spend your time editing the technical progress and value narrative rather than staring at a blank version of it.

HuddleActivities.Name: Assemble the technical review package
HuddleActivities.Description: Create a repeatable customer-review package.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Assemble a technical customer-review package from approved sources: executive technical summary, architecture and delivery progress, consumption or adoption evidence, optimization actions, material risks, open decisions, commitments and follow-through tracker. Preserve source links and flag missing or contradictory evidence.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved source package and reviewers.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Structured technical-review package.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSA reviews with relevant account, success, technical and commercial contributors.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Most of the effort in the technical review package is assembly, and assembly is exactly what AI removes.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build the specialist, technical, partner, and funding plan
HuddleActivities.Description: Clarify role coverage, dependencies, asks, owners, partner/funding needs, and decision checkpoints.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Create a pursuit orchestration plan for [opportunity] with customer outcome, solution scope, required specialist and technical roles, partner need, funding consideration, dependencies, owner for each action, decision checkpoints, and unresolved risks. Do not represent funding as approved.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved opportunity, customer context, roles, partner criteria, funding context, and constraints.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Pursuit orchestration plan with owners and checkpoints.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP validates role need, ownership, partner or funding involvement, and commitments.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Pursuits stall when handoffs, partner asks, or funding dependencies are assumed rather than owned.

HuddleActivities.Name: Make each ask specific enough to be accepted
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn a role requirement into an ask a busy colleague can say yes to without a meeting to clarify it.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: From this pursuit orchestration plan [paste], write the individual ask for each role involved. Each ask must state: what specifically is needed, why this pursuit needs that role rather than someone else, what the person receives from me to make it easy, the date it is needed by, and how long it should take. Keep each ask under 80 words. Do not represent funding, approvals, or customer commitments as secured if the plan does not show them as secured.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Bring the orchestration plan.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Check each ask states a realistic time commitment.
4. Send the asks.
5. Record who accepted.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The pursuit orchestration plan; the roles required; what you can supply to each; the customer timeline.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: One short, specific, dated ask per role, ready to send.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP verifies that no ask overstates funding, approval, or customer commitment status, and owns what is promised in return.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: A vague ask gets a polite yes and no calendar time.

HuddleActivities.Name: Catch the checkpoint that quietly slipped
HuddleActivities.Description: Compare the plan against what has actually happened and surface the dependency nobody has mentioned in two weeks.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Here is the pursuit orchestration plan with its checkpoints and owners [paste], and here is what has actually happened since [paste updates, meeting notes, or status]. Identify every checkpoint that has passed without evidence of completion, every dependency that has gone quiet, and every owner who has not confirmed. Rank by impact on the customer timeline. For the top item, draft the one message that would restart it. Do not assume something is complete because it was not mentioned.
HuddleActivities.ActivitySteps:
1. Bring the plan and recent activity. If the plan has no dated checkpoints or owners recorded, spend five minutes writing them down first; the activity does not work without them.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Confirm which items are genuinely stalled.
4. Send the restart message for the top one.
5. Reset the checkpoint date.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: The orchestration plan with checkpoints and owners, written down even if only informally; recent updates, notes, or status; the customer timeline. If checkpoints and owners do not exist yet, create them before running this activity.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: A ranked list of stalled checkpoints and quiet dependencies, plus one message to restart the highest-impact item.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: SSP confirms an item is genuinely stalled rather than simply undocumented before escalating to an owner.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Pursuits rarely stop. They go quiet, and quiet looks like progress until the date arrives.

HuddleActivities.Name: Analyze consumption and technical blockers
HuddleActivities.Description: Connect customer and sales context to technical trajectory.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Show consumption versus target for [Account], flag blockers, and recommend architecture, partner, or specialist actions that could improve the technical trajectory. Distinguish source facts from recommendations.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Account; target period; available MSX and customer context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Consumption gap and blocker view with candidate actions.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS validates consumption interpretation, architecture actions, partner need, and customer context.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The technical trajectory should respond to the blockers that are actually slowing value.

HuddleActivities.Name: Research technical options and bets
HuddleActivities.Description: Compare technical options and evidence before setting trajectory.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Analyze the main pipeline and consumption drivers for [Account] and recommend the top three technical bets. For each include business outcome, stakeholder, security posture, AI workload readiness, adoption blocker, first conversation, and validation gap. Separate sourced evidence from recommendations.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Account strategy; pipeline or consumption context; authorized sources.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Three evidence-backed technical bets with validation gaps.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS validates evidence, feasibility, strategic fit, and recommended priority.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Technical bets should be chosen on evidence, not novelty.

HuddleActivities.Name: Delegate the technical strategy package
HuddleActivities.Description: Build a bounded strategy and validation package.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the approved account context, technical bets, and source materials, create a technical strategy package with objectives, current estate, decision criteria, priority bets, proof needs, owners, milestones, risks, and open technical decisions.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved account context, technical evidence, and constraints.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Technical strategy package with decisions, owners, proof needs, and milestones.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS validates strategy, architecture, ownership, milestones, and customer relevance.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: You should spend time editing the strategy, not staring at a blank version of it.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build the technical decision path
HuddleActivities.Description: Connect approved account and customer context to the technical decision.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: For [Customer/opportunity], summarize outcome, current technical decision, stakeholders, recent interactions available, blockers, commitments and opportunity stage. Propose a decision path with evidence required, gaps, owners, milestones and next customer-facing action. Show source signals and flag unavailable context.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Authorized scope and approved technical context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Grounded technical decision path.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSA validates customer context, technical accuracy, owners, relevance and commitments.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Most of the effort in the technical decision path is assembly, and assembly is exactly what AI removes.

HuddleActivities.Name: Design the validation and proof plan
HuddleActivities.Description: Create a bounded validation plan.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the approved technical decision brief, build the smallest useful validation plan for [decision]. Include criteria, hypothesis, evidence available, proof gaps, activities, success measures, exit criteria, owners, milestones, dependencies, risks and expected decision. Do not expand beyond what is necessary.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved decision brief; owner; constraints; evidence.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Validation plan.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSA confirms scope, feasibility, criteria, evidence quality and ownership.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Settling the validation and proof plan before the work starts is the only version of that decision that holds.

HuddleActivities.Name: Design the executive briefing experience
HuddleActivities.Description: Plan an end-to-end executive briefing experience.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Help me organize an EBC for [Customer]. Choose the right session design and propose a coherent timeline and prep plan. Include desired customer decisions, executive audience, participants, evidence, role contributions, preparation milestones, risks, and follow-through.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Customer; executive audience; desired decisions; approved context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: EBC plan with session design, participants, evidence, timeline, and follow-through.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS validates purpose, participants, technical narrative, evidence, and customer decision.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: An EBC only works if the decision, people, evidence, and follow-through line up.

HuddleActivities.Name: Adjust the talk track from current signals
HuddleActivities.Description: Adapt approved technical messaging using selected work context.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the approved account brief, recent meetings, email, and technical source materials, identify the customer signals that should change the technical talk track. Draft revised opening language, five questions, likely objections, and responses. Separate sourced facts from recommendations.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Selected authorized work sources and approved technical narrative.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Revised technical talk track grounded in selected signals.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS validates signal interpretation, technical accuracy, customer relevance, and claims.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The talk track should change when the customer signal changes.

HuddleActivities.Name: Translate architecture into business value
HuddleActivities.Description: Create a concise business-value summary from approved architecture content.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Turn this reference architecture into a one-page business value summary. Map technical choices to customer priorities, expected business outcomes, Azure consumption implications, risks, and assumptions requiring review. Quantify only when the source supports it.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved reference architecture and supporting evidence.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: One-page technical-to-value summary with review flags.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS validates ROI, consumption impact, technical accuracy, and evidence.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Architecture matters more when the customer can see the business consequence.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build the run-of-show and evidence pack
HuddleActivities.Description: Turn the approved briefing plan into the run-of-show the session is actually delivered from.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the approved EBC plan, build the run-of-show: each segment in order with its time allocation, the person leading it, the evidence or demonstration used, the questions put to the customer, and the decision the session closes on. Assume the plan, participants and objectives are already agreed.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved EBC plan, confirmed participant list, and approved evidence.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Run-of-show with segment order, timing, owners, evidence, customer questions, and the closing decision.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS confirms every piece of evidence is approved for customer use and that each segment owner has agreed to their part.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The plan says why the briefing exists. The run-of-show is what the room is actually delivered from.

HuddleActivities.Name: Rehearse the strategic technical talk track
HuddleActivities.Description: Practice the technical conversation and receive coaching.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Use Agent J.ai to role-play the upcoming strategic technical conversation with [customer or stakeholder]. Use the approved narrative and focus on technical outcomes, open decisions, likely objections, evidence, and the technical ask. Pause for my response before coaching me on clarity, listening, evidence, and next step. Do not invent customer facts or commitments.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved narrative; meeting type; customer context; desired decision.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Interactive rehearsal, likely questions or objections, coaching, and improvement actions.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS validates customer facts, technical claims, commitments, evidence, and any response used with the customer.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Ten minutes rehearsing the talk track is cheaper than improvising it in the room.

HuddleActivities.Name: Prepare the CxO technical briefing
HuddleActivities.Description: Build an account-grounded executive technical briefing.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Prepare a CxO technical briefing for [Account] on [Topic]. Include customer outcomes, architecture direction, risks, proof points, executive talking points, likely questions, and the technical ask. Cite source signals where available and flag unsupported claims.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Account; topic; desired decision; available MSX and customer context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: CxO technical briefing with risks, proof points, talking points, and ask.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS validates architecture, risk, proof, customer context, and technical ask.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: The executive technical narrative needs enough evidence to be credible and enough focus to drive a decision.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build the executive technical deck
HuddleActivities.Description: Create a bounded executive-ready presentation package.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Build a concise executive technical deck for [Account] aligned to stated outcomes and the Azure or AI roadmap. Include the story arc, proof, architecture implications, risks, open technical decisions, and review flags.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved emails, transcripts, roadmap, and source materials.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Executive technical deck with open decisions flagged.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS reviews all claims, roadmap statements, evidence, and participant-facing content.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Deck creation should be assembly work; judgment stays in the story, claims, and ask.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build a technical health evidence brief
HuddleActivities.Description: Synthesize approved technical context.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using approved sources for [Customer], build a technical health brief. Separate verified evidence from assumptions. Summarize architecture and delivery state, material technical risks, optimization opportunities, open commitments, dependencies and missing evidence. End with the three issues that most deserve CSA attention and why.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved customer technical sources; review period; customer outcome.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Technical health brief.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSA validates architecture, delivery, support, usage interpretation, priorities and commitments.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Most of the effort in a technical health evidence brief is assembly, and assembly is exactly what AI removes.

HuddleActivities.Name: Prioritize a technical risk response
HuddleActivities.Description: Analyze enabled certified data relevant to technical health.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: For [Customer] and [period], identify the most material enabled consumption, usage or adoption changes visible in this report. Show supporting metrics, distinguish evidence from interpretation, state what the report cannot answer, and suggest which signals warrant deeper technical review. Do not assign a health score or infer customer intent.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Enabled certified report; customer; period.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Evidence-backed signals and technical-review priorities.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: CSA confirms report, filters, KPI meaning, technical significance and action.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Deciding a technical risk response is really deciding what you will not do. Say it out loud.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the technical V-team alignment brief
HuddleActivities.Description: Align technical roles, dependencies, priorities, and owners.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Using the approved account and technical context, create a V-team alignment brief with customer outcome, priority workloads, technical decisions, risks, required roles, dependencies, owner for each action, and next checkpoint. Flag unsupported assumptions.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Approved account and technical context; role list; decision needs.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Technical V-team alignment brief with owners and checkpoints.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS validates role need, ownership, dependencies, risk, and customer relevance.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Most work stalls in the handoff, not the task.

HuddleActivities.Name: Assess ECIF investment opportunities
HuddleActivities.Description: Identify whether ECIF funding could accelerate technical outcomes.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Review Opportunity ID [ID]. Using the customer architecture roadmap, consumption goals, and current deployment blockers: identify where ECIF funding could accelerate time-to-value, recommend relevant funding motions, explain expected customer outcome and directional consumption impact, and highlight risks, dependencies, or reasons ECIF may not be appropriate.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Opportunity ID; architecture roadmap; consumption goals; deployment blockers.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Prioritized ECIF funding opportunities with outcomes, impact, risks, and dependencies.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS and ECIF owner validate eligibility, funding motion, technical feasibility, consumption assumptions, dependencies, and recommendation before action.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Investment belongs in the v-team discussion when it removes a blocker to the technical strategy.

HuddleActivities.Name: Monitor ECIF investment performance
HuddleActivities.Description: Evaluate milestone progress, deployment readiness, and consumption path.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Analyze the proposed ECIF-funded engagement for Opportunity ID [ID]. Evaluate scope, milestones, deliverables, technical outcomes, Azure consumption goals, deployment path, risks, dependencies, and priority fixes. Provide a readiness assessment and name the decision owner.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Opportunity ID; proposed engagement; scope; milestones; deliverables; technical outcomes; consumption goals.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Engagement-quality assessment, gaps and risks, consumption-readiness assessment, and priority fixes.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS and ECIF owner validate scope quality, feasibility, consumption path, partner and customer readiness, compliance dependencies, and final funding decision.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Realization is judged on evidence someone collected or did not collect.

HuddleActivities.Name: Prioritize AI and Azure workloads
HuddleActivities.Description: Convert enabled business insights into a workload action list.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Turn this week’s business and technical signals into a prioritized AI and Azure workload action list. For each workload include readiness, potential impact, ACR or consumption upside if supported, blockers, owner, due date, and validation gap.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Enabled Proactive Insights, MSXI data, account context, and candidate workload list.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Prioritized workload action list with rationale, owner, and date.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS validates readiness, feasibility, upside interpretation, owner, and priority.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: This converts workload interest into a decision list with owners.

HuddleActivities.Name: Research workload readiness evidence
HuddleActivities.Description: Investigate technical and external evidence before prioritization.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Investigate [candidate workloads] for [Account]. Compare customer objectives, current estate, security posture, AI readiness, dependencies, adoption blockers, relevant external evidence, and validation gaps. Separate sourced facts from recommendations.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Account context; candidate workloads; authorized internal and public sources.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Evidence brief supporting workload prioritization.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS validates source quality, relevance, architecture implications, and recommendation.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Research is useful when it exposes why a workload is ready, blocked, or not worth chasing yet.

HuddleActivities.Name: Create the technical risk register
HuddleActivities.Description: Organize technical risks using available account and business data.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Build a weekly technical risk register for my account scope. Include affected accounts, opportunities, workload, MCEM stage, signal source, risk, likely impact, mitigation owner, and 14-day action. Flag unavailable context.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Enabled MSXI or sales data; ATS account scope.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Technical risk register with owner and action horizon.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS validates risk significance, technical context, owner, and mitigation.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Unnamed technical risk does not get owned.

HuddleActivities.Name: Build the account intelligence brief
HuddleActivities.Description: Combine work and public context into a meeting-prep brief.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: Act as my account intelligence analyst for [Account]. Build a meeting prep brief that summarizes business priorities, current technical strategy, stakeholder context, relevant KPIs, AI and Azure workload signals, open risks, recent customer commitments, and the top actions I should consider. Separate sourced facts from hypotheses and flag missing context.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Account; authorized email, Teams, calendar, files, CRM or sales context, and approved public context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: Account intelligence and meeting-prep brief with risks, priorities, and actions.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS validates current account context, stakeholder interpretation, technical risk, and customer relevance.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: Account intelligence is useful when it changes the next technical decision, not when it creates a longer dossier.

HuddleActivities.Name: Explain the KPI and locate the report
HuddleActivities.Description: Clarify the certified KPI or report behind the business signal.
HuddleActivities.Prompt: How is [KPI] calculated? Link me to the relevant report and explain the methodology, filters, and limits I should understand before using it in account technology planning.
HuddleActivities.RequiredContext: Enabled MSXI report or metric context.
HuddleActivities.ExpectedOutput: KPI definition, methodology, relevant report, and caveats.
HuddleActivities.HumanCheckpoint: ATS confirms that the KPI, scope, and report match the business question.
HuddleActivities.WhyThisMatters: If the signal is misunderstood, every technical priority built on it is suspect.
